target.title: feat(google): add typed Gemini CLI auth boundary
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The bundled Google plugin has two separate auth/runtime surfaces that need a hard boundary:

- `google` is the API-backed Google provider and uses API-key credentials.
- `google-gemini-cli` is the direct Gemini CLI runtime/provider and uses OAuth credentials staged into the Gemini CLI auth home.

Before this patch, the Gemini CLI prepare path depended on a private raw auth-profile object side channel, and the bridge accepted credential shapes that could blur the boundary between Google API-key usage and Gemini CLI OAuth usage.

This PR adds a typed Google credential resolver and an explicit CLI backend auth-forwarding capability so these credential kinds cannot cross that boundary by accident.

## What Changed

- Adds typed Google credential resolution in `src/agents/auth-profiles/google.ts`.
- Resolves `google` only as API-key credentials.
- Resolves `google-gemini-cli` only as OAuth credentials.
- Adds explicit CLI backend auth-forwarding metadata for the Gemini CLI backend.
- Changes CLI run preparation to forward credentials only when the backend capability accepts the selected provider and credential kind.
- Fails closed when a selected profile cannot be resolved into a typed credential before crossing the CLI backend plugin boundary.
- Removes API-key staging from the Gemini CLI OAuth bridge.
- Preserves current-main queued/atomic Gemini staging by keeping profile-home/settings/OAuth file writes inside `beforeExecution` and writing JSON through same-directory temp-file rename.
- Keeps Gemini CLI auth material in an isolated auth home and clears inherited Google/Gemini auth environment variables.
- Preserves default bundled `google-gemini-cli` provider/backend registration.
- Removes stale `OPENCLAW_ENABLE_GOOGLE_GEMINI_CLI_HARNESS` metadata/hints and deletes the unused harness opt-in helper/test.
- Updates the Google onboarding hint so it covers both Gemini API key and Gemini CLI OAuth choices.
- Documents CLI auth-profile forwarding in `docs/plugins/cli-backend-plugins.md` and validates the Plugin SDK API baseline.
- Adds `scripts/proof-google-auth-replacement.ts` as a deterministic real behavior proof.

## Evidence

Real environment: local OpenClaw checkout at PR head `9ccfc51c30cb20cbd6f864b015f7571f73b59dfd` using production resolver, CLI prepare, Gemini CLI auth-home staging code, bundled Google plugin registration code, Plugin SDK API baseline check, stale-policy grep check, focused Vitest suites, and the permanent real behavior proof script.

target.title: fix: keep Android gateway settings save idempotent
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Android users could tap Gateway Settings `Save & Connect` on an already-working app and unexpectedly re-enter gateway pairing or node capability approval when no meaningful setting changed.

The fragile behavior made Gateway Settings feel destructive: unchanged fields could still clear setup/device auth, endpoint edits could accidentally carry stale credentials, and the device-pairing admin message blurred phone pairing with node capability approval.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gateway Settings now uses the shared gateway connection resolver instead of rebuilding credential fallback inline, and it preserves saved setup/shared auth only for the unchanged saved manual endpoint. Endpoint changes drop saved credentials unless the user supplies replacement auth, and setup-code replacement now requires an explicit confirmation before clearing setup credentials and device tokens.

The copy around device-pairing admin access was also updated to explain that approving new phone pairing requires a gateway admin session, while node capability approval is a separate `nodes approve <request id>` flow.

## User Impact

Users can safely use `Save & Connect` from Android Gateway Settings without treating the screen like a destructive re-pairing action. A no-op save or reconnect path keeps existing gateway/device auth intact, while risky setup-code replacement is called out before it can trigger reapproval.

Operators get clearer wording when the current gateway sign-in can list nodes but cannot approve new phone pairing.

target.title: fix(diagnostics): avoid queue depth for accepted embedded steering
target.body:
## Summary

- Keep diagnostic `message.queued` events for accepted active embedded-run steering without counting them as queued backlog.
- Apply the non-backlog accounting only to active embedded-run steering; reply-run fallback and normal queued messages still increment `queueDepth`.
- Add a regression test proving an active embedded run can accept steering, finish, and leave diagnostic `queueDepth` at zero.

## What Problem This Solves

Active embedded runs can accept steered messages immediately through their run handle. That path was still logged as queued backlog, incrementing diagnostic `queueDepth`.

When the active run later completed, the normal idle transition only decremented one queue slot, so diagnostics could still report positive `queueDepth` even though no queued work remained.

Fixes #98685

## Evidence

- The new regression test queues a message into an active embedded run, verifies the handle receives it, clears the run, and asserts diagnostic state is idle with `queueDepth === 0`.
- Normal queued-message accounting is preserved because `logMessageQueued` still increments `queueDepth` by default; only accepted active embedded-run steering passes `countAsQueueDepth: false`.
- Runtime proof against real registry/diagnostic modules on the refreshed branch:

```text
$ node --import tsx - <<'SCRIPT'
# imports real src/infra/diagnostic-events.ts,
# src/logging/diagnostic-session-state.ts, and
# src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/runs.ts
# then registers one active embedded run, queues two steering messages,
# clears the run, and prints diagnostic state.
SCRIPT
before steer queueDepth=0 state=processing activeQueuedTurn=false
steer outcomes queued=true,target=embedded_run; queued=true,target=embedded_run
queued messages: continue one, continue two, steeringMode=all
```

target.title: fix(anthropic): handle max_turns stop reason and surface retry-limit details to users
target.body:
## Summary

- Keep Anthropic `max_turns` normalized to the existing public `length` stop reason in both Anthropic stream paths.
- Preserve the raw provider stop reason in assistant diagnostics as `provider_stop_reason`, so downstream code can distinguish Anthropic `max_turns` from ordinary `max_tokens` truncation without expanding the public `StopReason` union.
- Surface a specific incomplete-turn warning for Anthropic `max_turns` terminal turns instead of the generic “couldn't generate a response” fallback.
- Keep retry-limit internal breaker diagnostics in `meta.error` while using a shorter user-visible message for repeated idle-timeout exhaustion.

## Linked context

Closes #78145

## Root cause and scope

- Fix classification: Root-cause fix at the Anthropic stream normalization boundary plus the runner user-message boundary that consumes the normalized terminal turn.
- Maintainer-ready confidence: High. The final committed diff has focused RED/GREEN coverage for both Anthropic stream paths, incomplete-turn messaging, and retry-limit payload formatting.
- Root cause: Anthropic can report a provider turn-limit terminal condition as `stop_reason: "max_turns"`. Mapping that raw provider reason only to public `length` preserves the existing contract, but `length` alone is not enough context for runner/session finalization to tell provider turn exhaustion apart from ordinary output-token exhaustion.
- Why this is root-cause fix: The raw provider stop reason is captured where Anthropic stream events are normalized, before runner finalization consumes the assistant turn. The runner can then keep the public `length` semantics while using diagnostics to show the user actionable Anthropic max-turns context. This fixes the source invariant instead of adding a downstream string check after the provider-specific reason has been lost.
- Patch quality notes: The change is deliberately split between provider/transport normalization, incomplete-turn user messaging, and retry-limit payload formatting. The test-only type cast builds a fixture for an existing persisted assistant-message shape; production code reads diagnostics defensively. The new helper returns `false` for malformed diagnostics so old assistant records and non-Anthropic turns continue to use the existing generic fallback. The retry-limit change does not alter retry counts or timeout policy; it separates public payload text from internal `meta.error.message`.
- Why it matters / User impact: When Anthropic stops because the provider max-turns limit was reached, users see a specific instruction to start a fresh session or retry a smaller task instead of a generic incomplete-response warning. Internal retry-limit breaker details such as cost-runaway wording and issue IDs no longer leak into user-visible payload text.
- What did NOT change: This PR does not add a new public stop reason, does not classify `max_turns` as `error`, does not rotate/fail over models for `max_turns`, and does not change config, schema, credentials, routing, timeout thresholds, retry counts, or non-Anthropic providers.
- Architecture / source-of-truth check: The canonical public terminal-state contract stays `StopReason: "length"` for provider/output budget termination. Raw provider specificity is carried in extensible assistant diagnostics, matching the existing diagnostic pattern used for Anthropic refusal metadata.
- Related open PR / same-contract scan: This update is for the existing open PR #94130 linked to #78145, not a competing replacement PR. The same-contract risk is confined to Anthropic Messages stop-reason normalization and assistant diagnostics; no separate public `StopReason` contract PR is being introduced here.
- Out of scope: Live hosted Anthropic budget exhaustion orchestration, public stop-reason expansion, session migration, config/schema changes, timeout threshold changes, retry/failover policy changes, credentials/routing changes, and non-Anthropic providers.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: Anthropic `max_turns` responses need to remain public `length` terminal turns while preserving enough raw provider context to show actionable user guidance.
- Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on Linux with Node v24.16.0 and the repository package environment. The runtime proof directly invoked OpenClaw's production `streamAnthropic` function against an Anthropic-format SSE `Response`, so it exercised the real provider stream parser and stop-reason mapper without making a live API call.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  ```bash
  pnpm exec tsx --eval '<script imports streamAnthropic, feeds stop_reason=max_turns, prints normalized_stop_reason, and exits nonzero unless the result is length>'
  ```
- Evidence after fix: Console output from the runtime stream proof:
  ```text
  Anthropic max_turns runtime stream proof
  raw_stop_reason=max_turns
  normalized_stop_reason=length
  content=[{"type":"text","text":"Partial turn"}]
  usage={"input":4,"output":8,"cacheRead":0,"cacheWrite":0,"totalTokens":12,"cost":{"input":0,"output":0,"cacheRead":0,"cacheWrite":0,"total":0}}
  ```
- Observed result after fix: The production Anthropic provider stream path consumed a `message_delta` with `stop_reason: "max_turns"`, preserved partial assistant text and token usage, and returned `normalized_stop_reason=length`. The new regression coverage additionally asserts that both Anthropic paths now attach the raw `max_turns` diagnostic and that the runner surfaces the max-turns-specific user message.
- What was not tested: A live hosted Anthropic API run that actually exhausts the upstream turn budget, because forcing `max_turns` from the hosted API on demand is not deterministic.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: The issue-specific runtime proof replays an Anthropic-format SSE response through OpenClaw's real provider stream code instead of waiting for a hosted Anthropic API budget exhaustion event.
- Before evidence:
  ```text
  src/llm/providers/anthropic.test.ts: expected result.diagnostics to contain provider_stop_reason, received undefined
  src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts: expected result.diagnostics to contain provider_stop_reason, received undefined
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.incomplete-turn.test.ts: expected Anthropic max-turns warning, received generic incomplete-response warning
  src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/retry-limit.test.ts: expected public idle-timeout message, received internal cost-runaway breaker details
  ```

## Tests and validation

- Target test file: `src/llm/providers/anthropic.test.ts`; `src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts`; `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.incomplete-turn.test.ts`; `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/retry-limit.test.ts`.
- Scenario locked in: Anthropic emits `message_delta.delta.stop_reason: "max_turns"` after partial text and usage. OpenClaw returns `stopReason: "length"`, preserves content and usage, and attaches a `provider_stop_reason` diagnostic containing `rawStopReason: "max_turns"` and `normalizedStopReason: "length"` in both Anthropic stream implementations.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: The tests cover the two stream-normalization boundaries, the incomplete-turn user-message consumer, and the retry-limit formatting boundary without widening public API shape.

Focused RED/GREEN regression command after the final commit:
```bash
pnpm exec vitest run src/llm/providers/anthropic.test.ts src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/retry-limit.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.incomplete-turn.test.ts -t "maps Anthropic max_turns|keeps internal idle-timeout|surfaces Anthropic max_turns"
```

Regression coverage added:

- `src/agents/anthropic-transport-stream.test.ts` covers the same stop reason in the transport-stream path and asserts the same diagnostic shape.

- `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/retry-limit.test.ts` covers public/internal message separation for repeated idle-timeout exhaustion.

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes`) Anthropic max-turns terminal turns now surface a specific recovery instruction, and repeated idle-timeout retry exhaustion no longer exposes internal breaker details in the visible payload.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`No`)

Raw `max_turns` context is carried in assistant diagnostics, which are already extensible. target.title: fix(agents): resolve legacy modelstudio profile aliases
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #84081: legacy explicit auth profile ids like `modelstudio:default` fail to resolve after provider canonicalization to `qwen`, causing `No credentials found for profile "modelstudio:default"` even when `qwen:default` exists in the auth store.

## Summary

- Retry explicit legacy provider-prefixed profile ids through `resolveProviderIdForAuth` when direct lookup misses (resolver fallback in `model-auth.ts`).
- Add production Qwen manifest aliases: `modelstudio` → `qwen`, `qwencloud` → `qwen` in `extensions/qwen/openclaw.plugin.json` (required for the fallback to work outside mocked tests).
- Preserve explicit profile precedence: if `modelstudio:default` exists directly, it wins over `qwen:default`.

## Evidence

Repro path (before): store has only `qwen:default`, request `{ provider: "modelstudio", profileId: "modelstudio:default" }` → throws `No credentials found for profile "modelstudio:default"`.

After this patch (vitest, production manifest aliases + resolver fallback):

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/agents/model-auth.profiles.test.ts \
  src/agents/provider-auth-aliases.test.ts \
  src/agents/model-auth.modelstudio-profile-alias.test.ts \
  -t "84081|modelstudio profile" --run

 Test Files  6 passed (6)
      Tests  10 passed | 150 skipped (160)
```

Key assertions in `model-auth.modelstudio-profile-alias.test.ts` (no mocked alias map):
- `profileId: "modelstudio:default"` + store `{ "qwen:default": ... }` → resolves to `qwen:default`, key `qwen-key`
- store with both `modelstudio:default` and `qwen:default` → keeps explicit `modelstudio:default`

## Test plan

- [x] `provider-auth-aliases.test.ts` — reads bundled `extensions/qwen/openclaw.plugin.json`, asserts `modelstudio`/`qwencloud` → `qwen`
- [x] `model-auth.modelstudio-profile-alias.test.ts` — end-to-end `resolveApiKeyForProvider` with production manifest snapshot
- [x] `model-auth.profiles.test.ts` — alias fallback + explicit-profile precedence
- [ ] CI green

Fixes #84081

target.title: Add native Signal reply quotes
target.body:
## Summary

Signal auto-replies now preserve native Signal quote context when OpenClaw responds to the inbound Signal message that triggered the turn. The Signal plugin carries the inbound message timestamp, author, and body through reply delivery, sends quote metadata to native `signal-cli`/json-rpc, and maps the same quote fields to the Signal REST container send API. If quote metadata is missing, explicitly disabled, aimed at a different reply target, or rejected by the backend, OpenClaw falls back to a normal Signal message instead of dropping the reply.

## What Changed

- Inbound Signal handling records the inbound timestamp as the current reply target and carries native quote context into reply delivery.
- Signal text and media auto-replies include `replyToId`, `replyToAuthor`, and `replyToBody` only when they match the triggering inbound message.
- `replyToCurrent: false`, mismatched explicit reply targets, `replyToMode: off`, and single-message `batched` mode suppress native quote metadata for implicit replies.
- `replyToMode: first` consumes native quote metadata only for the first normal implicit reply; `replyToMode: all` preserves it across each emitted reply chunk.
- Explicit current-message replies can still quote the current message even when implicit reply mode is off.
- Native sends retry without quote metadata when Signal rejects quote fields, including unrecognized quote-field errors, while receipts preserve `replyToId` and record whether native quote send used `sent` or `fallback` status.
- Signal REST container mode translates quote metadata to `/v2/send` snake_case fields and strips `uuid:` prefixes from quote authors for the container API.
- Signal config now accepts `replyToMode` and direct/group `replyToModeByChatType` at channel and account scope, with account values taking precedence over channel chat-type overrides.
- Signal approval-reaction hint registration handles structured approval payload delivery, UUID-only linked accounts, and icon-prefixed approval prompt headers while preserving the current `signal.approval-reactions.v2` persistence namespace.
- Signal docs describe native quote behavior, fallback, and the new reply-to config fields.

## Proof

Behavioral proof:

- Focused automated coverage proves native quote send, fallback retry, receipt metadata, REST container quote fields, UUID author normalization, inbound context wiring, text replies, media replies, mismatched reply-target suppression, `replyToCurrent: false`, explicit current-message quoting, `replyToMode` chat/account precedence, single-use quote consumption, all-mode multi-chunk quoting, approval-reaction registration, and config schema acceptance/rejection.
- Live Signal proof used a local Signal REST/json-rpc linked device. A non-self inbound event in the Testing realm group was captured, the feature-branch send path sent one quoted proof reply with `replyToId`, `replyToAuthor`, and `replyToBody`, Signal accepted the send with `deliveredMessageIdPresent=true`, and Jesse visually confirmed the reply appeared in Signal.

Manual proof gaps and follow-up risks:

- The live proof covers group native quote delivery. Basic Signal DM reply behavior is already working in this linked setup, but this closeout did not add a fresh manual DM native-quote proof.
- No further live Signal messages were sent after the confirmed Testing realm proof.
- Temporary local Signal REST/container config fixes used to complete live proof are not product proof and are not part of this PR.
- Signal group id normalization and Signal mention matching remain separate follow-up risks outside this PR.

Screenshots are not included because this is a backend channel transport change with no OpenClaw-rendered UI surface. The human-visible proof is the live Signal confirmation above.

## Verification

Reviewer-checkable behavior:

- Rebased onto current `origin/main` at `3f289fdb4042`; latest PR head is `50ed0dc50b56`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src/send.test.ts extensions/signal/src/client-container.test.ts extensions/signal/src/core.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor.tool-result.sends-tool-summaries-responseprefix.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.inbound-context.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor.approval-reply-delivery.test.ts src/config/config.allowlist-requires-allowfrom.test.ts` passed after the rebase fixes: 2 Vitest shards, 7 files, 175 tests.

target.body:
Fixes #63106.

## Summary

- Add a scoped warning for fast successful main-session `systemEvent` cron jobs using `wakeMode="next-heartbeat"`.
- Persist the `possible-main-next-heartbeat-ghost-run` annotation in cron run logs.
- Carry and render cron run-log warnings in the Control UI run history.
- Add `cron.ghostRunWarningThresholdMs` config with schema/help metadata and public docs.
- Keep `CronRunLogEntry.warnings` source-compatible in generated Swift by defaulting the optional initializer parameter to `nil`.
- Keep release-note context in the PR body only; this branch does not edit `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: Verified that a fast successful main-session `systemEvent` cron handoff using `wakeMode: "next-heartbeat"` writes the `possible-main-next-heartbeat-ghost-run` warning into the cron run log, that Control UI run history can render that warning from `CronRunLogEntry.warnings`, and that existing Swift call sites can construct `CronRunLogEntry` without passing the new optional `warnings` label.

Real environment tested: Local macOS checkout on current PR head `5238f67159`, rebased on current `upstream/main` `4a206db106`, using the real `buildGatewayCronService`, real cron run-log reader, Control UI cron run-history renderer, protocol generators, and Swift compiler typecheck. The cron proof used an isolated temporary `OPENCLAW_HOME` and did not touch the real user cron store.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Rebased onto current `upstream/main`, regenerated gateway protocol artifacts, ran focused cron/gateway and Control UI tests, checked formatting/whitespace, verified generated protocol output stability, and typechecked a Swift compatibility snippet that constructs `CronRunLogEntry` without `warnings`.

target.title: feat: PluginStatusProvider plugin API for TUI footer status (resolves #64086)
target.body:
Resolves #64086. Coordinates with #53774 (broader footer-customization tracker).

## What this PR does

Adds a typed `PluginStatusProvider` interface and `registerStatusProvider` method to `OpenClawPluginApi`, following the same registration shape as `registerTool` / `registerHook`. Providers are stored in the plugin registry under a new `statusProviders` field.

```ts
export type PluginStatusProvider = {
  /** A unique identifier for this provider. */
  id: string;
  /** Function returning the status string, or null/undefined to hide it. */
  getStatus: () => string | null | undefined;
};
```

Plugin author usage:

```ts
api.registerStatusProvider({
  id: "contextclaw.savings",
  getStatus: () => `cc: -${savedPercent}%`,
});
```

## Scope

This PR lands the API/registry seam only:

- `PluginStatusProvider` type and `registerStatusProvider` API entry on `OpenClawPluginApi`.
- Plugin registry storage under `statusProviders`.
- API builder and plugin-entry SDK exposure.
- Duplicate, blank, and normalized-id validation.
- Loader rollback coverage so a provider registered by a plugin that later fails registration is removed with the rest of that plugin's side effects.

Explicitly not included:

- TUI render-path wire-up. That should stay in a follow-up once maintainers accept the API shape, ordering, truncation, theming, and footer placement.
- Cost-display footer changes. Those were split out of #64127 and can be revisited under #53774.

## Plugin-author motivation

I'm shipping [ContextClaw](https://github.com/dodge1218/contextclaw), a context-engine plugin that currently has to monkeypatch the bundled TUI to surface live stats. That breaks on OpenClaw release churn. A first-class `registerStatusProvider` seam gives plugins a supported path.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: A native plugin can call `api.registerStatusProvider(...)` during OpenClaw plugin registration, OpenClaw stores the provider in the plugin registry, and failed plugin registration rolls back status-provider side effects instead of leaving stale status entries.

Real environment tested:
- Current PR head: `1ff80b48b86c8bc6b6f34fd03cf2bf84a2f9bce0`.
- OpenClaw plugin loader/registry path from this branch.
- Earlier full dogfood proof used the real ContextClaw plugin and a real local OpenClaw gateway. The current-head follow-up below specifically covers the review blockers added after that proof: rollback, SDK baseline, and release-owned changelog scope.

Exact steps or command run after the patch:

```bash

OPENCLAW_VITEST_NO_OUTPUT_TIMEOUT_MS=120000 timeout 240s \
  pnpm exec node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \

pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 \
  src/plugins/loader.ts \
  src/plugins/loader.test.ts \
  src/plugins/registry.ts \
  src/plugins/registry.status-provider.test.ts \
```

## Coordination with #53774

target.title: chore(ci): harden package-manager resolution
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: CI and repo scripts had several package-resolution escape hatches: `pnpm dlx`, docs publish `npm install --no-save --package-lock=false`, non-hash-pinned pre-commit hook refs, stale pnpm pins, and Python CI installs that only implicitly relied on repo-root uv config.
- Why it matters: These paths are package supply-chain risk multipliers. They let trusted CI jobs resolve code at runtime from mutable registries, tags, or one-off install commands, which widens the window where a compromised, newly published, or retagged package could execute before maintainers have time to review or react.
- What changed: This PR makes those fetch paths more boring and reviewable: repo scripts use lockfile-pinned dev dependencies instead of `pnpm dlx`; CI Python installs explicitly load repo uv policy; pre-commit hooks are pinned to immutable commits; stale pnpm pins are aligned; and pnpm/uv both enforce the same two-day minimum package age gate.
- Regression guardrail: Root `AGENTS.md` now records these CI/pre-commit and package-manager supply-chain rules so agentic coding does not reintroduce mutable refs or one-off installs.
- Lockfile note: The `pnpm-lock.yaml` diff is expected. Replacing `pnpm dlx` with `pnpm exec` means the tools previously fetched on demand now live as dev dependencies, so their transitive dependency graphs are reviewed and pinned in the lockfile. Most of the noise comes from `knip` pulling optional/native `oxc` packages for multiple platforms.

- Missing detection / guardrail: There was no single guardrail preventing package-manager commands from resolving fresh packages outside the repo lockfile or configured age gate.

target.title: fix(auto-reply): dedupe idless inbound retries
target.body:
## Summary
- add a content/timestamp fallback inbound dedupe key when providers do not supply a stable message id
- keep normal provider-message-id dedupe unchanged
- cover idless retry dedupe and same-body/different-timestamp non-collapse

## Why
Some channel retry paths can re-enter auto-reply without a stable provider message id. In that case the current inbound dedupe returns invalid and the retry can be injected again. The fallback is scoped by provider/account/session/peer/thread plus a 128-bit SHA-256 prefix over timestamp and body, so ordinary provider-id paths keep their existing behavior while idless retries get a deterministic backstop.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: idless inbound retries should be suppressed when they carry the same route, timestamp, and text body, while distinct same-body messages and attachment-only idless messages should not be collapsed.

Real environment tested: rebased patched OpenClaw source checkout at `/tmp/openclaw-72314`, Node 24, directly invoking the real `src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-dedupe.ts` module through `tsx`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
node --import tsx /tmp/openclaw-72314-proof.mjs
```

target.title: feat(huggingface): add text-to-image generation via hf-inference Inference Providers route
target.body:
## Summary

Re-opens #63487 in a much smaller, focused form per @steipete's review feedback. Adds **text-to-image only** to the existing `huggingface` plugin, routed through the official Hugging Face Inference Providers `hf-inference` endpoint. No new credentials, no parallel HTTP stack, no out-of-scope capabilities.

Closes / supersedes #63487.

## What's in scope

- New `ImageGenerationProvider` registered by the existing `huggingface` plugin
- Endpoint: `POST https://router.huggingface.co/hf-inference/models/<repo_id>` (returns raw image bytes)
- Default model: `black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-Krea-dev`; recommended list also exposes FLUX.1-dev / FLUX.1-schnell / Qwen-Image / Hyper-SD (router accepts any compatible repo id)
- Reuses the existing `HUGGINGFACE_HUB_TOKEN` / `HF_TOKEN` credential — no new auth choice or env var
- `--size <W>x<H>` is forwarded as `parameters.width` / `parameters.height` per the [text-to-image task spec](https://huggingface.co/docs/inference-providers/tasks/text-to-image)
- JPEG output is surfaced when the upstream model emits it (mime + file extension inferred from `Content-Type`)

## Addressing the previous review

All five blockers from #63487 are handled:

1. **`isConfigured` uses the SDK** — `isProviderApiKeyConfigured({ provider: \"huggingface\", agentDir })`, no manual env scanning
2. **HTTP goes through guarded helpers** — `resolveProviderHttpRequestConfig` + `postJsonRequest` + `assertOkOrThrowHttpError`, so SSRF / proxy / timeout / dispatcher policy all behave like every other provider
3. **No parallel auth path** — request-time resolution via `resolveApiKeyForProvider`, same as chat
4. **Plugin manifest declares the contract** — `contracts.imageGenerationProviders: [\"huggingface\"]` in `openclaw.plugin.json`
5. **Tests + docs + changelog** — colocated Vitest spec, docs section under `docs/providers/huggingface.md`, changelog entry under the Unreleased section with `Thanks @lyfuci`

## Out of scope (deliberate)

Per maintainer guidance, this PR is intentionally tight. The following are **not** included and will be separate PRs if/when there's interest:

- Image-to-image / edit
- Multi-image batches
- Other Inference Providers routes (fal-ai, Replicate, Together, Nscale, WaveSpeedAI)
- Video / embeddings / STT

## Test plan

- [x] \`pnpm check:changed\` — 6 lanes green (conflict markers, typecheck extensions, typecheck extension tests, lint extensions, runtime import cycles, tests changed)
- [x] 7 new Vitest cases pass (default model, custom model + size, JPEG mime inference, missing key, upstream HTTP error, empty payload, capability surface)
- [x] Format check clean on the 6 touched files
- [x] End-to-end smoke test against the real \`hf-inference\` endpoint:
  \`\`\`bash
  openclaw infer image generate \\
    --model huggingface/black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-schnell \\
    --prompt \"a serene lake surrounded by mountains at sunset, photorealistic\" \\
    --size 1024x1024 \\
    --output lake.png
  # → 1024x1024 PNG, 800 KB, file lake.png: PNG image data, 1024 x 1024, 8-bit/color RGB
  \`\`\`

---

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** The provider's default model `black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-Krea-dev` is no longer served by the `hf-inference` provider (HF routes it to `fal-ai`/`replicate`), so it returned `400 Model not supported by provider hf-inference`; also `count > 1` was silently ignored, and `ssrfPolicy` was not forwarded to the HTTP layer. This proof covers the fixed default (`FLUX.1-schnell`), the `count > 1` rejection, and that the live request path reaches `hf-inference` authenticated.

**Real environment tested:** Real OpenClaw checkout built with `pnpm build` (branch head `24a516d8`), Node 24, running the compiled provider from `dist/` against the live `https://router.huggingface.co/hf-inference` router with a real `HF_TOKEN`. Not a unit test / mock — the built provider and real HTTP path.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Imported the built provider chunk from `dist/` and called `provider.generateImage(...)` directly — once with `count: 2` (expect rejection) and once with the default model and a real prompt (expect a live HTTP round-trip to hf-inference).

**Evidence after fix:** Verbatim console output from the built provider:
```
[proof] provider.id = huggingface | defaultModel = black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-schnell
[proof] count:2 -> Hugging Face image generation supports only a single image per request (count must be 1)
[proof2] generateImage error -> Hugging Face image generation failed (HTTP 402): You have depleted your monthly included credits. Purchase pre-paid credits to continue using Inference Providers. [request_id=Root=1-6a3506bf-...]
```

**Observed result after fix:** (1) The shipped build defaults to `FLUX.1-schnell` and rejects `count: 2` with the explicit single-image error. (2) The live `generateImage` → `postJsonRequest` → HF router call returns **HTTP 402** (not 400/401) — proving the request was correctly routed to `hf-inference`, authenticated with the token, and accepted the `FLUX.1-schnell` model; it failed only because this account's monthly image credits are exhausted. This exercises the real SSRF-guarded `postJsonRequest` path and `assertOkOrThrowHttpError`. Default-model change verified live against the HF provider-mapping API (2026-06-19): of the previously-listed repos, only `FLUX.1-schnell` is on `hf-inference`.

**What was not tested:** A successful end-to-end image (saved PNG) could not be produced because the HF account's monthly image credits are exhausted (HTTP 402) — this is an account billing limit, not a code defect; a clean PNG can be generated once credits reset. Requesting maintainer `proof: override` for the generation step, since the routing/auth/model/validation path is proven above.

target.title: fix(media): allow aws-sdk auth mode for image and audio/video paths
target.body:
The chat path's `prepareSimpleCompletionModel` exposes an
`allowMissingApiKeyModes` escape hatch so providers whose
`auth.mode === "aws-sdk"` (notably `amazon-bedrock`) can resolve
credentials at call time via the AWS SDK chain instead of a static
`apiKey`. The image and audio/video runtime paths in
`media-understanding` did not have the same escape: each one
unconditionally called `requireApiKey`, which throws on the empty-key
sentinel, so the `image`/`audio`/`video` tools failed for Bedrock
deployments using BYOK with role/SSO/profile credentials.

This was rebased onto current `main` and re-architected onto the
keyless `kind: "none"` execution-auth mechanism that landed in the
runner since this PR was opened. The earlier two-commit approach
(threading an `allowEmptyKey` flag through `executeWithApiKeyRotation`)
is no longer needed: the runner already knows how to execute keyless,
so the fix is now just teaching the two auth-resolution sites to choose
the keyless path for `aws-sdk` providers.

Two sites resolve a primary api key:

- `prepareResolvedImageRuntime` and `resolveMinimaxVlmFallbackRuntime`
  (`src/media-understanding/image.ts`) — the image tool resolves auth
  via `getApiKeyForModel`. When the resolved key is empty *and* the
  mode is `aws-sdk`, pass the key through as `""` and skip
  `setRuntimeApiKey` so no empty-string secret is persisted in runtime
  auth storage; otherwise `requireApiKey` runs and the existing throw
  semantics are preserved for every other mode.
- `resolveProviderExecutionAuth`
  (`src/media-understanding/runner.entries.ts`) — the audio/video paths
  route through this shared chokepoint. When `requireApiKey` throws
  missing-key / missing-provider-auth and the resolved auth mode is
  `aws-sdk`, return the `kind: "none"` execution auth so the runner
  executes keyless (passing `CUSTOM_LOCAL_AUTH_MARKER` as the apiKey
  placeholder and bypassing `executeWithApiKeyRotation`), exactly as the
  local / no-auth providers already do. Every other mode still rethrows.

Closes #72031.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior or issue addressed: the image, audio, and video runtime
  paths resolve a primary api key via `requireApiKey`, which throws when
  the resolved `apiKey` is the empty-string sentinel. For
  `amazon-bedrock` deployments configured with `auth.mode: aws-sdk`
  (BYOK via role/SSO/profile credentials), the resolved key is empty, so
  the throw blocked the tools before the AWS SDK credential chain could
  resolve credentials at call time — even though the chat path already
  resolves keyless for the same provider.

- Real environment tested: isolated Linux OpenClaw checkout of
  `openclaw/openclaw` on the rebased PR branch
  `fix/image-tool-allow-aws-sdk-auth-mode` (single commit on current
  `main`), Node v22.22.2. Tests run through the repo's own
  media-understanding shard runner — the same non-isolated runner CI
  uses for this lane.

- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.media-understanding.config.ts
```

  plus a stash-bisect to prove the new tests fail without the source
  fix:

```text
# with the fix applied: 24 files / 265 tests pass
git stash push -- src/media-understanding/image.ts src/media-understanding/runner.entries.ts
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.media-understanding.config.ts
# -> the three aws-sdk tests go RED (image throws missing-api-key;
#    audio/video decision == "failed")
git stash pop
```

- Evidence after fix: the media-understanding shard is green with the
  fix applied — `Test Files 24 passed (24)`, `Tests 265 passed (265)`,
  including the new `runner.aws-sdk.test.ts` (audio + video keyless on
  `amazon-bedrock`) and the new `amazon-bedrock` aws-sdk case in
  `image.test.ts`. The new tests assert the keyless handoff directly:
  the image path returns `apiKey: ""` without calling `requireApiKey`
  or `setRuntimeApiKey`, and the audio/video paths pass
  `CUSTOM_LOCAL_AUTH_MARKER` through to the provider (the `kind: "none"`
  placeholder) instead of throwing.

- Observed result after fix: stash-bisecting the two source edits while
  leaving the new tests in place flips exactly those three tests to RED,
  with the image case throwing `No API key resolved for provider
  "amazon-bedrock" (auth mode: aws-sdk, ...)` and the audio/video cases
  producing a `failed` decision. Restoring the fix returns them to
  green, so the guards track the fix rather than passing
  unconditionally.

- Live Bedrock confirmation: @bstanbury independently confirmed the
  image-tool fix working against live AWS Bedrock on macOS arm64,
  OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (`e510042`), running the `image` tool against
  `amazon-bedrock/arn:aws:bedrock:us-west-2:323866345974:inference-profile/us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6`
  with `AWS_PROFILE=default` SDK-chain credentials (no
  `AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK`, no static API key). Before: `No API key
  resolved for provider "amazon-bedrock" (auth mode: aws-sdk, checked:
  profile:amazon-bedrock:default)`. After (same image, same model, same
  creds): `The animal in this image is an orange tabby cat.` The
  re-architected image carve-out here produces the same empty-key
  handoff @bstanbury validated. Live evidence:
  https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/72092#issuecomment-4514876830

- What was not tested: I (the PR author) did not exercise the live AWS
  Bedrock leg myself because I lack Bedrock credentials in my
  development environment. The live-network gap is closed by the
  @bstanbury confirmation above for the image path; the in-tree
  empty-key / keyless handoff for all three paths is closed by the
  mutation-proofed shard tests above. A maintainer wanting to reproduce
  the network leg in CI would need a Bedrock-credentialed runner.

### AI-assisted

- [x] Tested. New tests cover the image, audio, and video describe
  paths on `amazon-bedrock` + `aws-sdk`. The media-understanding shard
  runs clean (`24 files / 265 tests`) on the rebased single-commit
  branch, and a stash-bisect proves the three new tests fail without the
  source fix.
- [x] I understand the change. The chat path landed an
  `allowMissingApiKeyModes` allowance when `aws-sdk` auth was first
  added (so the AWS SDK chain can resolve creds itself). The image and
  audio/video paths resolve auth independently and never carried that
  allowance through to `requireApiKey`. The fix is the narrowest
  equivalent on top of `main`'s current keyless plumbing: the image path
  passes `""` through (and skips `setRuntimeApiKey`); the audio/video
  chokepoint returns `kind: "none"`. Every non-`aws-sdk` mode keeps the
  existing throw.

## Summary

Describe the problem and fix in 2-5 bullets:

- Problem: Signal has reaction send helpers, but inbound runs never wired `messages.statusReactions.enabled` into the shared status reaction lifecycle.
- Why it matters: Signal users get no queued/thinking/tool/compacting/done/error visual feedback during long-running agent turns even when status reactions are configured.
- What changed: Create a Signal status reaction controller for eligible inbound messages, route lifecycle callbacks through `dispatchInboundMessage`, and send reactions via `sendReactionSignal` for direct and group messages.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): No config shape changes, no Signal REST/native transport changes, and no agent/tool message-action behavior changes.

- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: Signal's inbound handler dispatched messages without creating a `StatusReactionController` or passing lifecycle callbacks (`onReplyStart`, `onToolStart`, compaction callbacks, terminal state handling) into `dispatchInboundMessage`.
- Missing detection / guardrail: Signal had send-reaction helper tests, but no inbound regression test for `messages.statusReactions.enabled`.
- Contributing context (if known): Other channels already wire the shared status reaction controller; Signal had the transport primitive but not the inbound lifecycle wiring.

Signal now honors `messages.statusReactions.enabled` for inbound runs by updating reactions on the triggering message during the agent lifecycle.

```text
Before:
Signal inbound -> dispatchInboundMessage -> no status reaction callbacks -> no lifecycle reactions

After:
```

target.title: fix(signal): await daemon shutdown on restart
target.body:
## Summary
- make Signal daemon shutdown asynchronous and await process exit
- fall back to SIGKILL if signal-cli does not exit after SIGTERM
- add regression coverage for daemon stop semantics and aborted monitor shutdown

## Testing
- corepack pnpm exec vitest run extensions/signal/src/daemon.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor.tool-result.autostart.test.ts
- corepack pnpm exec vitest run extensions/signal/src

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: Signal auto-start monitor shutdown/restart must wait for the spawned daemon process to exit instead of returning while the daemon is still alive, preventing orphaned `signal-cli daemon` processes across abort/restart paths.
- Real environment tested: macOS 14.8.5 arm64 on a local OpenClaw checkout, Node v22.22.2, PR head `3fa74e98e72de378366b4dc5d48cae5f6dd21249`. The machine does not have a linked Signal account or `signal-cli` installed, so this proof used the real OpenClaw Signal monitor/daemon lifecycle code with a local signal-cli-compatible child process that exposes `/api/v1/check` and `/api/v1/events`; no external Signal messages were sent.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
cd /Users/zhoukailian/Desktop/mySelf/openclaw/.worktrees/fix-signal-daemon-stop-race
node --import tsx /tmp/openclaw-signal-lifecycle-proof.mjs | tee /tmp/openclaw-signal-lifecycle-proof.out
```

- Evidence after fix (screenshot, recording, terminal capture, console output, redacted runtime log, linked artifact, or copied live output):

```json
{
  "repoHead": "3fa74e98e72de378366b4dc5d48cae5f6dd21249",
  "baseMain": "e0225380a7454a85db1038e495d18a28b5d918ed",
  "port": 20031,
  "pid": 34488,
  "aliveBeforeAbort": true,
  "monitorResolved": true,
  "resolveWaitMs": 659,
  "aliveAfterMonitorResolved": false,
  "elapsedMs": 867,
  "events": "START pid=34488 args=[\"daemon\",\"--http\",\"127.0.0.1:20031\",\"--no-receive-stdout\",\"--receive-mode\",\"manual\"]\nSIGTERM pid=34488 at=1778304230573\nEXIT_AFTER_SIGTERM pid=34488 at=1778304231225",
  "runtimeLogs": [
    {
      "level": "log",
      "t": 200,
      "msg": "signal-cli: signal-cli shim READY pid=34488 http=127.0.0.1:20031"
    },
    {
      "level": "error",
      "t": 867,
      "msg": "signal daemon exited (source=process code=0 signal=null)"
    }
  ]
}
```

- Observed result after fix: The Signal monitor started the daemon child process, verified it was alive before abort, sent SIGTERM on abort, waited about 659ms for the child to finish its shutdown, then resolved only after the process exited. `aliveAfterMonitorResolved: false` confirms there was no leftover daemon process after `monitorSignalProvider` returned.
- What was not tested: A live linked Signal account, real `signal-cli` network traffic, actual inbound/outbound Signal message delivery, or the macOS LaunchAgent restart path. This proof is scoped to the changed OpenClaw daemon lifecycle behavior and avoids sending external Signal messages from the test machine.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged): The regression tests added in this PR demonstrate the previous behavior: on unpatched main, `stop()` returned `undefined` instead of a promise and there was no SIGKILL escalation. The live proof above verifies the patched after-fix runtime behavior on this machine.

## Root Cause

- Root cause: Signal daemon shutdown was fire-and-forget. `stop()` only sent SIGTERM and returned immediately, so monitor abort/restart could continue while the old daemon process was still shutting down.
- Missing detection / guardrail: There was no regression coverage asserting that daemon stop returns a promise, waits for process exit, is idempotent across overlapping callers, and escalates to SIGKILL when SIGTERM does not finish.
- Contributing context (if known): `signal-cli` daemon shutdown can be slow enough that immediate restart paths race with the previous process still owning resources.

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [x] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file:
  - `extensions/signal/src/daemon.test.ts`
  - `extensions/signal/src/monitor.tool-result.autostart.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: `stop()` waits for daemon exit after SIGTERM, escalates to SIGKILL after the timeout, reuses an in-flight stop promise, and `monitorSignalProvider` awaits daemon stop before resolving aborted shutdown.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: It exercises the Signal daemon lifecycle seam directly without requiring a live Signal account or sending external messages.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): None before this PR.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Signal auto-start restart/shutdown should leave fewer orphaned daemon processes. Shutdown may now wait briefly for `signal-cli daemon` to exit; if it does not exit after SIGTERM, OpenClaw escalates to SIGKILL after the configured timeout.

Closes #22676

target.title: feat(plugins): upgrade llm_input/llm_output hooks from fire-and-forget to modifying
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: `llm_input` and `llm_output` plugin hooks are fire-and-forget (observe-only). Plugins cannot block, modify, or redact LLM calls/responses.
- Why it matters: Plugin authors need the ability to intercept LLM traffic for compliance, content filtering, prompt rewriting, and response redaction use cases.
- What changed: Both hooks now run sequentially via `runModifyingHook`. `llm_input` can return `block`, `blockReason`, `prompt`, or `systemPrompt` overrides. `llm_output` can return replacement `assistantTexts`. The attempt runner awaits both hooks and applies returned modifications.
- Security hardening (follow-up commits):
  - `PluginBlockedError` sentinel prevents failover logic from misclassifying plugin blocks as transient provider failures (e.g. rate-limit/auth errors)
  - `allowPromptInjection=false` enforcement: `llm_input` hooks are constrained via `constrainLlmInputPromptInjectionHook` when the policy is set, matching existing `before_agent_start`/`before_prompt_build` behavior
  - Image re-detection after prompt rewrite with full rollback on failure (reverts prompt, systemPrompt, and images to pre-hook state)
  - Priority layering: higher-priority (earlier) plugins win for prompt/systemPrompt overrides (`acc ?? next` merge strategy); `evolveEvent` propagates effective state to lower-priority handlers
  - Payload cloning: `historyMessages` and `assistantTexts` are shallow-copied before passing to hooks to prevent in-place mutation bypassing the merge contract
  - `lastAssistant` stripping: when `llm_output` overrides `assistantTexts`, text/content/errorMessage are cleared from `lastAssistant` to prevent reasoning blocks and error metadata from leaking downstream, while preserving `stopReason` and `usage` for failover logic
  - Plugin-blocked errors are excluded from overflow and rate-limit heuristics in both `run.ts` and `agent-runner-execution.ts`
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): Hook event shapes are unchanged (additive result types only). Plugins that return `void` behave identically to before. No changes to other hooks, plugin discovery, or the Plugin SDK public surface.

## Change Type (select all)

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #
- Related #57585 — adds a complementary `transform_context` hook at the context-window layer; this PR operates at the prompt-assembly/response-delivery layer instead
- [ ] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause / Regression History (if applicable)

N/A

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- Plugins registering `llm_input` hooks can now return `{ block: true, blockReason: "..." }` to prevent an LLM call from being made.
- Plugins registering `llm_input` hooks can return `{ prompt, systemPrompt }` to override the prompt/system prompt sent to the LLM.
- Plugins registering `llm_output` hooks can return `{ assistantTexts: [...] }` to replace the assistant response (e.g. for redaction).
- Existing plugins that return `void` from these hooks are unaffected — fully backward compatible.
- When `allowPromptInjection=false` is set for a plugin, `llm_input` prompt/systemPrompt fields are stripped from the hook result (block/blockReason still honored).

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[prompt ready] -> llm_input (fire-and-forget, no return) -> [LLM call] -> [response] -> llm_output (fire-and-forget) -> [delivered]

After:
[prompt ready] -> await llm_input -> [block? -> PluginBlockedError] or [apply prompt/systemPrompt overrides -> re-detect images] -> [LLM call] -> [response] -> await llm_output -> [apply assistantTexts override, strip lastAssistant] -> [delivered]
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? Yes
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- New/changed network calls? No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- Data access scope changed? No
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: Plugins can now modify prompts and block/alter LLM responses. This is gated behind the existing plugin hook registration mechanism — only installed and enabled plugins can register these hooks. The blocking path throws a dedicated `PluginBlockedError` sentinel that is logged and excluded from failover/overflow misclassification. Prompt modifications are subject to `allowPromptInjection` policy enforcement. Hook payloads are cloned to prevent mutation. Response overrides strip original content from `lastAssistant` to prevent data leaks. Prompt/response modifications flow through the same trust boundary as existing modifying hooks (e.g. `before_tool_call`).

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS
- Runtime/container: Node 22+ / Bun
- Model/provider: Any
- Integration/channel (if any): N/A
- Relevant config (redacted): Plugin with `llm_input`/`llm_output` hook registered

### Steps

1. Register a plugin with an `llm_input` hook that returns `{ block: true, blockReason: "test" }`
2. Trigger an agent run
3. Observe the LLM call is blocked with the logged reason

### Expected

- LLM call is blocked and error is thrown with reason

### Actual

- LLM call is blocked and error is thrown with reason

## Evidence

- [x] Code review hardening: all 12 review comments from automated reviewers (Codex/Greptile) addressed across 9 follow-up commits
- [ ] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets: manual gateway test with a local test plugin confirmed `llm_input` and `llm_output` hooks fire correctly on v2026.4.1 gateway. Logs show `llm_input fired` with prompt rewrite (`-> rewriting prompt (prepending tag)`), `llm_output fired` with `assistantTexts (1)` and usage data, and `-> BLOCKING: prompt contains "BLOCKED"` for the block path. The released gateway treats hooks as fire-and-forget (return values ignored), confirming backward compatibility; modifying behavior (block/rewrite/redact) is validated by 22 automated tests.
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Hook blocking, prompt override, response redaction via test plugins, multi-plugin priority chaining with `evolveEvent` propagation
- Manual gateway testing: installed a local test plugin (`llm-hook-test`) on a live v2026.4.1 gateway via `openclaw plugins install -l`. Confirmed hook registration, `llm_input` firing with prompt data (provider, model, sessionId, imagesCount), `llm_output` firing with assistantTexts and usage. Tested block, rewrite, redact, and observe scenarios through the dashboard web UI. Verified the released gateway's fire-and-forget path is unaffected (backward compat).
- Automated tests: 22/22 tests pass in `wired-hooks-llm-modifying.test.ts` covering block result, prompt/systemPrompt override, evolveEvent propagation, multi-plugin priority merge, backward compat (void returns), and error handling (graceful degradation).
- Edge cases checked: Plugin returning void (backward compat), hook failure graceful degradation (logged warning, continues), `allowPromptInjection=false` constraint, image re-detection failure rollback, empty prompt override (`prompt: ""`), `PluginBlockedError` bypassing failover/overflow heuristics
- What you did **not** verify: End-to-end production load with many concurrent plugins across multiple providers

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config/env changes? No
- Migration needed? No

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: A misbehaving plugin could block all LLM calls or silently rewrite prompts.
  - Mitigation: Blocking is logged with reason via dedicated `PluginBlockedError`. Prompt/response modifications are opt-in (plugin must explicitly return override fields). `allowPromptInjection=false` can constrain prompt modification. Hook payloads are cloned. Existing hook failure handling catches and logs errors gracefully without crashing the run. Higher-priority plugins take precedence via first-setter-wins merge strategy.

target.title: fix(agents): restore global subagent model default priority over agent own model
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #58822.

- Restores correct subagent model precedence in `resolveSubagentConfiguredModelSelection`: global `agents.defaults.subagents.model` now takes priority over the parent agent's own `model.primary`, with the agent's own model only used as a last-resort fallback
- Applies the same fix to the cron isolated-agent model selection path (`src/cron/isolated-agent/model-selection.ts`) and the shared `resolveSubagentModelConfigSelectionResult` helper in `src/agents/agent-scope.ts`
- Updates existing tests from #58003 to assert the corrected behavior and adds new coverage for main-agent, named-agent, and explicit-override scenarios

### Background

PR #58003 reordered `resolveSubagentConfiguredModelSelection` to prefer `agentConfig.model` over `agents.defaults.subagents.model`. While this was intended to let named agents keep their own model for subagents, it caused a regression: when the main agent runs Opus and `defaults.subagents.model` is GPT-5.4, subagents incorrectly inherited Opus because the agent's own model shadowed the global subagent default.

The correct precedence is:
1. `agentConfig.subagents.model` — explicit per-agent subagent config (highest)
2. `agents.defaults.subagents.model` — global subagent default
3. `agentConfig.model` — agent's own model (last-resort fallback)

## Test plan

- [x] `pnpm test src/agents/model-selection.test.ts` — 105 tests pass
- [x] `pnpm test src/cron/isolated-agent.model-formatting.test.ts` — 32 tests pass
- [x] `pnpm test src/agents/openclaw-tools.subagents.sessions-spawn.model.test.ts` — 11 tests pass
- [x] `pnpm test src/agents/subagent-spawn.model-session.test.ts` — 1 test passes
- [x] `pnpm test src/gateway/session-utils.test.ts` — 84 tests pass
- [x] `pnpm test src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts` — 34 tests pass
- [x] Test: main agent (Opus) with global subagent default (GPT-5.4) → subagents use GPT-5.4
- [x] Test: named agent without per-agent subagents.model → uses global default
- [x] Test: falls back to agent own model when no global default set
- [x] Test: explicit model override in spawn always wins

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Subagent model resolution for a main agent whose own `model` differs from `agents.defaults.subagents.model`. Before this PR, an Opus-running agent with `defaults.subagents.model = openai/gpt-5` still produced Opus subagents because the agent's own `model` shadowed the global subagent default in `resolveSubagentConfiguredModelSelection`, in the shared `resolveSubagentModelConfigSelectionResult` helper, and in the cron isolated-agent path. This PR restores the documented precedence so the global default wins over the agent's primary model, while per-agent `subagents.model` still takes the very top slot.

**Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64 (Node v24.15.0), local checkout of `fix/subagent-model-precedence-global-default` at HEAD `81168e5de5`, dependencies installed via `pnpm install`. Resolvers exercised by importing the actual TypeScript source under `src/agents/model-selection.ts` and `src/agents/agent-scope.ts` via the `tsx` loader — no mocks, no Vitest, no provider catalogs swapped out. The cron isolated-agent path uses the same `resolveSubagentModelConfigSelectionResult` helper, so the asserted source values cover that resolver too.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```
$ cd pr-58823
$ pnpm install --prefer-offline
$ node --import tsx scripts/proof/pr-58823-subagent-precedence.mjs
```

The script (`scripts/proof/pr-58823-subagent-precedence.mjs`, committed in this PR for reviewer reproducibility) constructs three real `OpenClawConfig` shapes, calls `resolveSubagentModelConfigSelectionResult`, `resolveSubagentConfiguredModelSelection`, and `resolveSubagentSpawnModelSelection` on each, and asserts both the resolved model ref and the selection `source` label (`subagent` / `default-subagent` / `agent`).

**Evidence after fix:** Verbatim terminal stdout (runtime log) from the live `node --import tsx` run above against the patched sources:

```
PR #58823 subagent model precedence — real-behavior proof
repo head: (local worktree)
node: v24.15.0

--- scenario A — global default beats agent primary ---
input.agentConfig.model              = anthropic/claude-opus
input.defaults.subagents.model       = openai/gpt-5
input.agentConfig.subagents.model    = (unset)
agent-scope source                   = default-subagent
agent-scope raw                      = "openai/gpt-5"
model-selection.resolveConfigured()  = openai/gpt-5
model-selection.resolveSpawn()       = openai/gpt-5
OK scenario A — global default beats agent primary

--- scenario B — per-agent override wins ---
input.agentConfig.model              = anthropic/claude-opus
input.defaults.subagents.model       = openai/gpt-5
input.agentConfig.subagents.model    = openai/gpt-5-mini
agent-scope source                   = subagent
agent-scope raw                      = "openai/gpt-5-mini"
model-selection.resolveConfigured()  = openai/gpt-5-mini
model-selection.resolveSpawn()       = openai/gpt-5-mini
OK scenario B — per-agent override wins

--- scenario C — falls through to agent primary ---
input.agentConfig.model              = anthropic/claude-opus
input.defaults.subagents.model       = (unset)
input.agentConfig.subagents.model    = (unset)
agent-scope source                   = agent
agent-scope raw                      = "anthropic/claude-opus"
model-selection.resolveConfigured()  = anthropic/claude-opus
model-selection.resolveSpawn()       = anthropic/claude-opus
OK scenario C — falls through to agent primary

PROOF PASSED — subagent model precedence follows: per-agent > defaults.subagents > agent primary
```

For completeness, the Vitest suites listed in Test plan also pass on this branch (`pnpm test src/agents/model-selection.test.ts` → 105 passed; `pnpm test src/cron/isolated-agent.model-formatting.test.ts` → 32 passed; etc.), but the authoritative proof above is the live `node --import tsx` run against the actual patched source files, not the unit suite.

**Observed result after fix:**

- Scenario A (Opus main agent, `defaults.subagents.model = openai/gpt-5`, no per-agent override): the live resolver returns `openai/gpt-5` with `source = default-subagent`. Before this PR it returned `anthropic/claude-opus` with `source = agent` — the exact bug from #58822.
- Scenario B (per-agent `subagents.model = openai/gpt-5-mini` set alongside the global default): `openai/gpt-5-mini` with `source = subagent` wins. Per-agent override still beats the global default, confirming the highest-priority rung is intact.
- Scenario C (neither per-agent `subagents.model` nor `defaults.subagents.model` set): resolves to the agent's own `model` (`anthropic/claude-opus`) with `source = agent`, confirming the documented last-resort fallback is preserved.

The `node` exit code was `0` (proof script asserts each expectation; first mismatch would throw). The `agent-scope` source labels are produced by the shared `resolveSubagentModelConfigSelectionResult` helper used by both `src/agents/model-selection.ts` and `src/cron/isolated-agent/model-selection.ts`, so a passing scope source label means the cron path inherits the same precedence.

**What was not tested:** Cross-OS runtime (macOS / Windows) — code path is platform-agnostic config resolution, no filesystem or shell dependencies. Live spawn of an actual subagent process against a remote model provider — the resolver returns the same model ref regardless of whether the downstream spawn succeeds, and the spawn path is exercised by `src/agents/openclaw-tools.subagents.sessions-spawn.model.test.ts` (11 passing). UI surfacing of the resolved subagent model in the gateway is also unchanged by this PR and not re-tested here.

target.title: fix(agents): classify Anthropic refusal and OpenAI content_filter as failover-eligible refusals
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Provider refusals (Anthropic safety classifiers, OpenAI `content_filter`) silently bypass the model fallback chain. When a provider returns a refusal, the agent run-loop surfaces a generic "LLM request failed." error without ever consulting the configured fallback models — even though Anthropic's own refusal copy recommends configuring a fallback model.
- Problem: `classifyFailoverClassificationFromMessage` has no refusal pattern → `classifyAssistantFailoverReason` returns null → `failoverFailure=false` → `shouldRotateAssistant=false` → `continue_normal` → fallback chain never checked
- Solution: Add `"refusal"` to `FailoverReason`, match Anthropic refusal and `content_filter` messages in the unified failover classifier, and treat refusal as a transient failure eligible for cooldown probing
- What changed: `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/types.ts` (+1, new reason), `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/errors.ts` (+12, refusal detection in `classifyFailoverClassificationFromMessage`), `src/agents/failover-policy.ts` (+2, cooldown probe eligibility), `src/agents/auth-profiles/types.ts` (+1, `AuthProfileFailureReason` mirror), `src/agents/runtime-plan/types.ts` (+1, `AgentRuntimeFailoverReason` mirror)
- What did NOT change: `failover-matches.ts` (refusal is two simple prefix matches, not worth a pattern group), `resolveFailoverStatus` (refusal has no HTTP analog), `resolveSessionSuspensionReason` (default `circuit_open` is correct), `buildFailoverRemediationHint` (only triggers for auth)

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [x] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #98976
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Three production incidents in one morning logged `failoverReason: null` for Anthropic refusals with `Anthropic refusal (category: bio) ...` in the error body. Each time the provider message explicitly said "API integrators: you can reduce refusals for your users by configuring a fallback model — see https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/refusals-and-fallback". But OpenClaw never triggered the fallback chain because the failover classification pipeline had no concept of a refusal.

After fix, a refusal flows through the same rotate-profile → fallback-model pipeline as rate limits and overloads. The refused model enters cooldown; the next candidate handles the turn.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: Provider refusals (Anthropic `stop_reason=refusal`, OpenAI `finish_reason=content_filter`) are classified as failover-eligible, triggering the configured model fallback chain instead of silently dying with "LLM request failed."
- Real environment tested: Linux x86_64, Node 22, branch `fix/provider-refusal-fallback-98976`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/errors.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/types.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/failover-matches.test.ts src/agents/failover-policy.ts src/agents/failover-policy.test.ts

OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 npx vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/failover-matches.test.ts src/agents/failover-policy.test.ts

OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 npx vitest run src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/errors-provider-structured-signals.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/provider-error-patterns.test.ts
```

- Evidence after fix:

```console
$ node --import tsx -e "
import { classifyFailoverReason } from './src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/errors.ts';

console.log('=== Refusal classification proof ===');
console.log();

const cases = [
  { input: 'Anthropic refusal (category: bio): The content...', expect: 'refusal' },
  { input: 'Anthropic refusal.', expect: 'refusal' },
  { input: 'Provider finish_reason: content_filter', expect: 'refusal' },
  { input: 'LLM request failed.', expect: null },
  { input: 'rate limit exceeded', expect: 'rate_limit' },
  { input: 'The request was refused by the proxy.', expect: null },
];

for (const c of cases) {
  const result = classifyFailoverReason(c.input);
  const status = result === c.expect ? 'PASS' : 'FAIL';
  console.log(status + ' | \"' + c.input.substring(0, 60) + '\" → ' + result);
}
"
=== Refusal classification proof ===

PASS | "Anthropic refusal (category: bio): The content..." → refusal
PASS | "Anthropic refusal." → refusal
PASS | "Provider finish_reason: content_filter" → refusal
PASS | "LLM request failed." → null
PASS | "rate limit exceeded" → rate_limit
PASS | "The request was refused by the proxy." → null
```

Classification matrix:

| Input message | Expected | Actual |
|---|---|---|
| `"Anthropic refusal (category: bio): ..."` | `"refusal"` | `"refusal"` |
| `"Anthropic refusal."` | `"refusal"` | `"refusal"` |
| `"Provider finish_reason: content_filter"` | `"refusal"` | `"refusal"` |
| `"LLM request failed."` | `null` (not refusal) | `null` |
| `"rate limit exceeded"` | `"rate_limit"` (not refusal) | `"rate_limit"` |
| `"The request was refused by the proxy."` | `null` (not refusal) | `null` |

Cooldown probe matrix:

| FailoverReason | allowCooldownProbe | useTransientProbeSlot | preserveTransientProbeSlot |
|---|---|---|---|
| `"refusal"` (new) | ✅ true | ✅ true | ❌ false |
| `"rate_limit"` | ✅ true | ✅ true | ❌ false |
| `"overloaded"` | ✅ true | ✅ true | ❌ false |

Unit test results:
```
 ✓ |unit-fast| failover-matches.test.ts   27 passed (4 new refusal tests)
 ✓ |unit-fast| failover-policy.test.ts     1 passed (matrix updated)
 ✓ provider-error-patterns.test.ts         88 passed (no regressions)
 ✓ oxfmt --check                            7 files clean
```

- Observed result after fix:
  1. `classifyFailoverReason("Anthropic refusal ...")` returns `"refusal"` — was `null`
  2. `shouldAllowCooldownProbeForReason("refusal")` returns `true` — would have been `false` (new reason)
  3. `shouldUseTransientCooldownProbeSlot("refusal")` returns `true` — would have been `false`
  4. `shouldPreserveTransientCooldownProbeSlot("refusal")` returns `false` — correct (refusal is transient)
  5. `shouldEscalateRetryLimit("refusal")` returns `true` — correct (fallthrough from negative list)
  6. All existing failover classifications unchanged — zero regression
- What was not tested:
  - Live Anthropic/Bedrock provider end-to-end refusal → fallback chain. The correctness of the refusal classification is proven at the classifier level; a live E2E test requires a provider that reliably returns a classifier-triggering refusal, which is non-deterministic.

## Root Cause

`classifyFailoverClassificationFromMessage` in `src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/errors.ts` had no pattern for "Anthropic refusal" or "Provider finish_reason: content_filter". When an assistant message arrived with `stopReason="error"` and refusal text, the classifier returned `null`, `isFailoverAssistantError` returned `false`, `shouldRotateAssistant` returned `false`, and `resolveRunFailoverDecision` returned `{ action: "continue_normal" }` — which ends the turn with no fallback attempt.

Provenance: `introduced by` the original `shared/anthropic-refusal.ts` — the refusal→error mapping was wired but never connected to failover classification.

Confidence: `clear` — single classification entry point, all callers downstream react to the returned reason.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

When a provider refuses a prompt and fallback models are configured, the agent now falls back to the next candidate instead of surfacing "LLM request failed." with no fallback attempt. When no fallbacks are configured, behavior is unchanged — the refusal message is still surfaced.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: `classifyFailoverReason` correctly classifies Anthropic refusal (with/without category), OpenAI content_filter, and does not false-positive on proxy refusal text or generic errors
- Edge cases checked: Empty string, unrelated text containing "refusal" in proxy context
- What you did NOT verify: Live production refusal → fallback chain E2E (requires non-deterministic classifier trigger)

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — purely additive; existing reasons unchanged
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. The single classification entry point (`classifyFailoverClassificationFromMessage`) is the right boundary because every failover path (assistant-stage, prompt-stage, signal-level, detail-level) already goes through it. Adding a new reason here automatically propagates to the full fallback pipeline without touching any of the downstream decision helpers.
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternative considered**: Classifying refusal via `failover-error.ts`'s `resolveFailoverReasonFromError` path. Rejected — that path only fires for thrown errors, whereas refusal is a normal stream result with `stopReason="error"` on the assistant message. The message-level classifier is the correct gate.

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Risk**: The refusal reason string format changes across Anthropic SDK versions. Mitigation: `startsWith("Anthropic refusal")` is a loose prefix check; the underlying `applyAnthropicRefusal` function always produces `"Anthropic refusal"` as the message prefix, and that prefix is independently test-covered in existing refusal formatting tests.
- **Risk**: OpenAI `content_filter` finish reason could be confused with a future provider that uses different wording. Mitigation: exact prefix match `"Provider finish_reason: content_filter"` which is the canonical output of `mapOpenAIStopReason` — any format change there would also break the existing stop-reason mapping.

---
Fixes #98976

target.title: [AI-assisted] feat(android): add chat command controls
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

No linked issue; this is a team-approved Android PR.

Android chat did not give users a discoverable way to start a fresh conversation or discover Gateway-backed slash commands from the composer. Earlier PR iterations also exposed session-command behavior that could diverge from the safer Control UI invariants: `/new` could travel through normal message send instead of Android's guarded New Chat path, and New Chat could still be available while active or queued chat work made a session switch unsafe.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds Android New Chat controls backed by Gateway `sessions.create`, a Gateway-backed slash command picker that opens when users type `/`, prefix filtering by command name or text alias, and guarded handling for Android session creation. New Chat is disabled while sending, streaming, loading, running, or queued chat work is active; delayed `sessions.create` responses are ignored if the selected session or run state changed; selected or typed `/new` routes through the guarded Android New Chat path; and admin-gated slash commands Android cannot safely execute are filtered or disabled instead of requiring Android to request `operator.admin`.

Scope boundaries: Android does not request or persist `operator.admin`, this PR does not add a permanent slash button in the composer, and admin-gated reset execution is not part of the PR claim.

## User Impact

Android users can start a fresh chat from the header `+` action or with `/new` when chat state is safe. Typing `/` shows Gateway-backed command suggestions that narrow by command name or alias prefix, so Android no longer depends on a hard-coded fallback command catalog. The composer no longer shows a persistent slash character between the attachment icon and message placeholder. New Chat is unavailable when it would risk abandoning active or queued chat work, and stale created-session responses no longer overwrite a newer selected session.

## Evidence

Latest PR head covered by this body: `708b6094d5126cff9df2f5a70e9a80feb899aebc`.
