target.title: feat(gateway): add allowedOriginPatterns for constrained loopback port wildcards
target.body:
Closes #98383

## What Problem This Solves

Remote WebView-hosted node clients (e.g. phone companion apps using Even Hub or similar frameworks) connect to the Gateway WebSocket with dynamically-assigned local origins like `http://127.0.0.1:<random-port>`. The current `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` only supports exact origins or the global `["*"]` wildcard, forcing users to choose between two inadequate options:

- **Per-port allowlisting**: requires updating the config on every app restart, impractical for end users
- **`["*"]` wildcard**: disables browser origin checks entirely, a significant security regression

## Why This Change Was Made

Added `gateway.controlUi.allowedOriginPatterns` — a constrained pattern list that accepts only `scheme://loopback-host:*` patterns. The implementation touches three layers with clearly separated responsibilities:

**1. Zod schema (config load time — fail-close)**

Each pattern must pass six checks: valid format (`scheme://host:*`), explicit protocol (`http:` or `https:`), port-level `*` wildcard only, no host wildcards, and hostname in the loopback literal set (`127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, `[::1]`). Illegal patterns prevent service startup — no silent downgrades.

**2. Runtime matching (`checkBrowserOrigin`)**

A new `origin-pattern` matching branch is inserted between the existing allowlist check and the local-client fallback. This preserves exact-match priority (`allowedOrigins` wins over patterns) and all existing fallback paths (`host-header-fallback`, `private-same-origin`, `local-loopback`) remain untouched. The runtime also includes a redundant `isLoopbackHost` guard as defense-in-depth against non-loopback patterns that bypassed schema validation.

**3. Startup config validation**

- `server-runtime-config.ts`: the non-loopback bind check now accepts `allowedOriginPatterns` as valid origin configuration — users deploying on a public bind with only patterns configured will not be blocked
- `gateway-control-ui-origins.ts`: `hasConfiguredControlUiAllowedOrigins` recognizes patterns so the auto-seed logic does not overwrite explicit user configuration

**4. Codex review follow-up**

- `schema.help.ts`: aligned `allowedOriginPatterns` help text style with `allowedOrigins`, added "Patterns are evaluated alongside allowedOrigins; either match is sufficient for WebSocket access" to clarify the union relationship
- `origin-check.test.ts`: added two HTTP trusted-proxy path tests confirming `allowedOriginPatterns` is correctly propagated through `resolveHttpBrowserOriginPolicy` → `authorizeTrustedProxyBrowserOrigin` → `checkBrowserOrigin`

**Design constraints preserved across the stack:**

- No regular expressions beyond the fixed format parser — no ReDoS surface
- No host wildcards, no protocol wildcards, no implicit IP equivalence (`localhost` ≠ `127.0.0.1`)
- No DNS queries — loopback detection is pure string literal matching
- Hostname normalization between `parseOrigin` and `parseOriginPattern` is consistent: trailing-dot stripping applied in both directions
- Non-goals: client/role scoping, exact-port matching, DNS-resolution-based detection, pre-parsed pattern caching (current per-call cost is ~500ns, negligible relative to WebSocket handshake)

## User Impact

Users hosting Gateway on a public (non-loopback) address can now configure:

```json
{
  "gateway": {
    "controlUi": {
      "allowedOriginPatterns": ["http://127.0.0.1:*"]
    }
  }
}
```

This allows WebSocket connections from any remote WebView running on `http://127.0.0.1:<any-port>` without resorting to `["*"]`. The full loopback family is supported (`127.0.0.1`, `localhost`, `[::1]`, both `http:` and `https:` protocols).

**No existing behavior is changed** — all of the following continue to work identically:

- `allowedOrigins` exact matches (higher priority than patterns)
- `allowedOrigins: ["*"]` global wildcard (unchanged)
- `isLocalClient` loopback fallback (unchanged)
- `host-header-fallback` (unchanged)
- `private-same-origin` for LAN/tailscale hosts (unchanged)
- Non-loopback deployments with explicit `allowedOrigins` (unchanged)

Users currently on `["*"]` for WebView support can migrate to `["http://127.0.0.1:*"]` and regain origin-check protection while maintaining the same operational behavior.

**Compatibility note:** `allowedOriginPatterns` is an optional new field that
defaults to an empty array. Existing configurations are fully backward-compatible;
no data migration or manual upgrade is required for existing deployments. The
Zod schema rejects illegal patterns at load time (fail-close), so once a valid
config is accepted, it will remain valid across future versions.

## Evidence

**Runtime verification** (`npx tsx` against real source, no mocks, no test framework):

```
30/30 tests passed

─── A: Zod Schema allowedOriginPatterns (11/11) ───
  ✅ A1: http://127.0.0.1:* accepted
  ✅ A2: http://localhost:* accepted
  ✅ A3: http://[::1]:* accepted
  ✅ A4: https://127.0.0.1:* accepted
  ✅ A5: non-loopback hostname rejected
  ✅ A6: exact port without * rejected
  ✅ A7: host wildcard http://*:* rejected
  ✅ A8: bare * rejected
  ✅ A9: ftp protocol rejected
  ✅ A10: empty patterns array accepted (no regression)
  ✅ A11: allowedOrigins + allowedOriginPatterns coexist

─── B: checkBrowserOrigin runtime matching (15/15) ───
  ✅ B1: http://127.0.0.1:40313 matches pattern [CORE ISSUE SCENARIO]
  ✅ B2: http://localhost:5173 matches http://localhost:*
  ✅ B3: http://[::1]:8080 matches http://[::1]:*
  ✅ B4: https://127.0.0.1:9000 matches https://127.0.0.1:*
  ✅ B5: http://127.0.0.1 (no explicit port) matches pattern
  ✅ B6: non-loopback origin blocked
  ✅ B7: localhost != 127.0.0.1 (no implicit equivalence)
  ✅ B8: protocol mismatch rejected
  ✅ B9: allowedOrigins exact match takes priority over patterns
  ✅ B10: existing * wildcard still works (no regression)
  ✅ B11: isLocalClient loopback fallback unchanged (no regression)
  ✅ B12: empty patterns does not create bypass
  ✅ B13: trailing dot normalization works (localhost. matches localhost)
  ✅ B14: first matching pattern in array wins
  ✅ B15: * in allowedOrigins + empty patterns still works

─── C: CSRF startup guard (4/4) ───
  ✅ C1: allowedOriginPatterns counts as configured origins
  ✅ C2: both empty → not configured (CSRF guard active)
  ✅ C3: allowedOrigins with values still works
  ✅ C4: host-header fallback still works
```

target.title: fix(telegram): distinguish and render streamed reasoning/commentary progress lanes
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves On Telegram, the streamed progress window (the live "thinking" preview shown while a reply is generated) was broken in several visible ways compared to Discord: 1. **Reasoning and commentary were indistinguishable.** Both lanes rendered plain, with no `🧠`/`💬` markers — a user watching a streamed turn could not tell the model's *reasoning* from its *commentary*. Discord renders reasoning italic under `🧠` and commentary upright under `💬`. 2. **Model Markdown leaked or was stripped.** `**bold**`, backticks, and `_…_` in lane text either surfaced as literal characters or were silently flattened to plain text. 3. **`
` broke every multi-line preview at the transport.** Progress drafts join rendered lines with `
`, but Bot API `parse_mode=HTML` has no `
` tag. Telegram rejected every multi-line preview edit with *"can't parse entities"*, and the parse-error fallback silently downgraded the whole draft to unformatted plain text — so streamed progress formatting effectively **never rendered** on non-rich accounts. 4. **No collapse summary.** When the window tore down, it left nothing behind — the streamed activity vanished with no digest of what happened. 5. **Window churn / scroll-jump.** The window was deleted and reposted on lane handovers, and on `/reasoning on` it repositioned below the durable reasoning block, yanking the client's scroll position up by pages and sometimes posting the final answer off-screen. 6. **Interim answer blocks streamed into the window.** Partial answer content leaked into the progress preview (Discord suppresses this). ## Why This Change Was Made Channel-side only (`extensions/telegram/**`); no core `src/**` changes. One focused commit per concern: 1. **Lane identity + rendering** — pass the `🧠`/`💬` lane prefixes and `commentaryItalics:false` to the shared progress-draft compositor (mirroring the Discord channel), and render lane bodies through `renderTelegramHtmlText` (the `parse_mode=HTML`-safe converter). Lane lines collapse to one line first (multi-line commentary otherwise forms block markdown — a `\n\n---\n\n` separator turns the paragraph above into a setext `

`, which Telegram rejects). Long lines clip **inside** the whole-line `_…_` wrapper so truncation cannot chop the closing underscore and degrade italic to plain. 2. **Transport** — convert `
` joins to literal newlines in the `parse_mode=HTML` transport branch, matching what the rich-message branch already does. 3. **Preview lifetime** — keep the streaming preview on screen ≥4s from first appearance before a teardown delete, scheduled detached (never awaited) so turn teardown is not stalled. 4. **Collapse summary bar** — on teardown, collapse the window **in place** (edit, not delete) into a one-line activity digest: `🧠 N thoughts · 💬 N notes · 🛠️ N tool calls · ⏱️ Ns`. Counts reflect **only streamed** content (durable `/verbose on` messages own their own delivery and are excluded — persistent-message XOR window-count invariant). 5. **Single stationary window** — one Telegram message per turn, edited through every lane handover; zero happy-path deletes. The final answer is delivered **before** the bar edit so the window never repositions below durable content (kills the scroll-jump). Rare repositions post-new-then-delete-old (deferred delete) instead of delete-then-repost. 6. **Interim answer-block suppression** — suppress partial answer blocks from the progress window (Discord parity). Non-goals: final-answer rendering and the durable (`/verbose on`) lanes are untouched — this is only the streamed progress window. ## User Impact Telegram users watching a streamed reply now see a formatted, stable progress window: reasoning (`🧠`, *italic*) clearly distinct from commentary (`💬`, plain), the model's Markdown rendered (bold step names, monospace commands) instead of leaking or being stripped, a stationary box that no longer deletes/reposts or jumps the scroll, and a persistent one-line activity digest left behind on collapse. Biggest improvement for deepseek, which narrates progress almost entirely through its markdown-heavy reasoning lane. ## Maintainer-ready classification - **Fix classification:** channel-local bug fix + small feature (collapse bar). Bounded to `extensions/telegram/**`; no core, no plugin-SDK, no config/default surface added, no new env var. - **Root cause:** the Telegram progress path never passed the compositor's per-channel lane markers, hand-escaped lane bodies instead of using the `parse_mode`-safe renderer, and emitted `
` into a `parse_mode=HTML` transport that has no such tag. The scroll-jump was a window-lifecycle defect (delete-then-repost across lane handovers). - **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** lane semantics come from the shared `createChannelProgressDraftCompositor` (`src/channels/progress-draft-compositor.ts`) — the same source Discord consumes; this change makes Telegram a consumer of that contract rather than diverging. The tool-count gate reuses the compositor's own public predicate `isChannelProgressDraftWorkToolName` (via `openclaw/plugin-sdk/channel-outbound`), so the bar's `🛠️` tally cannot drift from what the compositor actually renders. - **Sibling-surface check:** Discord is the mirror. Its summary bar (`deliverDiscordReply` → `sendDurableMessageBatch`) has **no transcript-mirror seam**, so the Telegram bar was hardened to match (see F1 below) — the invariant now holds identically on both channels. - **Patch quality:** `git diff --numstat` net prod LOC is small and localized; new files are `progress-summary.ts` (tracker + formatter) and its test. No new fallback readers, no config compat. - **Related-PR scan:** rebased onto current `main` (post-2026.7.1) including `b07fd6f1b4 fix(telegram): keep group history always on`; the only overlap was an import block (dropped the now-deleted `group-history-context` import, kept upstream's `selectTelegramGroupHistoryAfterLastSelf`). No open PR touches the progress-window path. ## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs) - **Behavior addressed:** streamed progress-window lane rendering, `
` transport, collapse summary bar, stationary-window (no scroll-jump), interim-answer suppression. - **Real environment tested:** dev gateway built from this exact branch head, Telegram Desktop, fresh session per turn (`/new`). - **Exact steps:** `/reasoning stream` + markdown-heavy prompt for the lane render; `/reasoning on` + `/verbose off` for the collapse-bar + stationary-window turn. - **Evidence (runtime capture):** **Summary bar + lane gating** (`/reasoning on`, `/verbose off`, gpt-5.5) — a single frame shows the collapse bar `💬 2 notes · 🛠️ 2 tool calls · ⏱️ 61s`, the durable 🧠 reasoning block rendered italic with bold/monospace preserved, and the correct gating: durable (`/reasoning on`) reasoning renders in full but is **not** counted in the bar, while streamed notes/tool calls **are** — matching the persistent-message XOR window-count invariant. ![summary bar + lane gating](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-telegram-progress-lanes/telegram-streamed-progress-lanes/pr-proof-6-summary-bar-collapse.png) **Lane rendering close-ups** (`/reasoning stream`, markdown-heavy prompt) — reasoning `🧠` italic with `**bold**` rendered bold-italic and backtick commands monospace, all inside the italic wrapper; commentary `💬` upright with bold step names and monospace commands (visual contrast with the italic reasoning): [🧠 reasoning zoom](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-telegram-progress-lanes/telegram-streamed-progress-lanes/pr-proof-2b-reasoning-zoom.png) · [💬 commentary zoom](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-telegram-progress-lanes/telegram-streamed-progress-lanes/pr-proof-3b-commentary-zoom.png) · full-stage: [prompt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-telegram-progress-lanes/telegram-streamed-progress-lanes/pr-proof-1-prompt.png) · [🧠 reasoning](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-telegram-progress-lanes/telegram-streamed-progress-lanes/pr-proof-2-reasoning-italic.png) · [💬 commentary](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-telegram-progress-lanes/telegram-streamed-progress-lanes/pr-proof-3-commentary.png) · [💬 step 3](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Marvinthebored/openclaw/proof-assets-telegram-progress-lanes/telegram-streamed-progress-lanes/pr-proof-4-commentary2.png) - **Observed result:** `🧠` reasoning renders italic with bold/monospace preserved inside the wrapper; `💬` commentary renders upright; the window stays a single stationary message and collapses in place into `🧠 N thoughts · 💬 N notes · 🛠️ N tool calls · ⏱️ Ns`; the final answer arrives before the bar with no scroll-jump. - **What was not tested:** streamed reasoning-lane italics were exercised on a reasoning-bearing provider in an earlier build and by unit tests; the latest sanity turn used a model that emitted empty reasoning, so its *streamed-🧠 italic* frame is covered by the unit suite + the earlier live capture rather than the final sanity capture. Group DM / forum-topic progress windows were not separately re-captured (unaffected by this change). - **Proof limitations:** captures are from a dev gateway on a developer Telegram account (names/emails redacted), not a production deployment. ## Red-team hardening (this branch) An adversarial pass produced 5 findings, all fixed in `fix(telegram): red-team hardening for the progress collapse bar`: - **F1 (HIGH) — transcript pollution.** The bar was mirrored into the model's session transcript (`durable:true` → `transcriptMirror`), so the model could read its own cosmetic activity digest back as a prior turn. Discord's bar has no such seam. Fix: `mirrorTranscript:false` on the two bar sends; real finals keep mirroring. - **F4 — tool overcount.** The bar's `🛠️` counter incremented on non-work tools (`message`/`reply`/etc.) before the compositor's work-tool gate. Fix: gate the count with `isChannelProgressDraftWorkToolName` + `toolProgress` so the tally matches what the window renders. - **F2 — silent collapse drop.** `finalizeToPreview` ignored a failed edit (flood-wait 429). Fix: return `undefined` so the caller falls back to a durable bar post. - **F3 — unguarded cosmetic send.** A throw in the cleanup-fallback bar send could fail the turn. Fix: try/catch + `logVerbose`. - **F5 (LOW) — ghost-preview race.** A first send racing a reposition could orphan a bubble. Fix: `repositionedSendGenerations` guard deletes the late-landing send deferred. Follow-up (ClawSweeper review finding): F3 originally guarded only the *cleanup* fallback bar send. The *normal* path (`applyProgressCollapseSummary`) awaited an unguarded durable send when `finalizeToPreview` could not edit in place, and `sendPayload` throws on delivery failure — so a cosmetic bar flood-wait could fail an otherwise-complete turn (`merge-risk: message-delivery`). Both cosmetic-bar sends now route through one shared guarded helper `postCosmeticSummaryBar` (swallow + `logVerbose`); added the regression for the no-live-message fallback send throwing while the final answer still delivers. ## Tests and validation - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-telegram.config.ts extensions/telegram/src/{bot-message-dispatch,draft-stream,progress-summary}.test.ts` → **239 passed** (3 files). New coverage: lane markdown rendering in both lanes, clipped-long-reasoning stays italic, multi-line commentary stays `parse_mode`-safe (the setext-`

` trap), `
`→newline transport, ≥4s dwell timing, collapse-bar counts/format, stationary-window reposition + deferred-delete, one test per red-team finding (F1 mirror-absent, F4 counts, F2 failed-edit fallback, F3 throw-swallow, F5 reposition-race), and both cosmetic-bar fallback sends throwing without failing the turn (cleanup + no-live-message paths). - Rebased clean onto current `main` (post-2026.7.1); telegram suites green on the rebased head. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

target.title: fix(zai): add User-Agent header to endpoint detection probe
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: z.ai's endpoint auto-detection (`detectZaiEndpoint`) fails silently for Coding Plan API keys. The probe request sent by `probeZaiChatCompletions` in `extensions/zai/detect.ts` lacks a `User-Agent` header. z.ai's edge infrastructure rejects User-Agent-less requests with HTTP 429 (error code 1305: "The service may be temporarily overloaded"), causing all detection probes to fail and the function to return `null`. As a result, new users onboarding with z.ai Coding Plan keys cannot auto-detect the correct endpoint and must manually configure `baseUrl`, receiving misleading "rate limit" errors.

**Solution**: Add a `User-Agent` header to the `probeZaiChatCompletions` request, using the existing `openclaw/${version}` format already established in `src/agents/auth-profiles/usage.ts` and `src/infra/provider-usage.fetch.codex.ts`. The version is sourced from `process.env.OPENCLAW_VERSION` with a `"dev"` fallback when the environment variable is not set, matching the pattern established in `usage.ts`. The fix is purely additive — one header line in an existing request.

**What changed**: `extensions/zai/detect.ts` — added `const version = process.env.OPENCLAW_VERSION?.trim()` and `"user-agent": \`openclaw/${version || "dev"}\`` to the probe headers (2 lines). `extensions/zai/detect.test.ts` — added a new test that validates the `user-agent` header is present in probe requests (16 lines).

**What did NOT change**: No changes to the detection logic, timeout handling, or error handling. No changes to any other provider's endpoint detection. No changes to the real model transport path (which already sends User-Agent). No new dependencies, no API surface changes.

Fixes #98100

---

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**:
Users onboarding z.ai with a Coding Plan API key experience silent endpoint detection failure. `detectZaiEndpoint` returns `null`, the config falls back to the standard `https://api.z.ai/api/paas/v4` endpoint, and the Coding Plan key (which is only authorized on the coding endpoint `https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4`) gets HTTP 429 on every real call. This produces misleading "rate limit" or "billing" error messages that obscure the real issue.

**Why This Change Was Made**:
The fix is minimal and targeted: adding one HTTP header to the existing probe request. Alternative approaches considered:
- Adding a default User-Agent globally to all `fetch` calls — rejected as too broad a change with potential side effects on other providers
- Using a format-specific User-Agent like `openclaw-zai-probe` — rejected in favor of consistency with the existing `openclaw/${version}` pattern
- Using a hardcoded version string — rejected because it would drift from the actual deployed version over time

The chosen approach is the simplest possible change that resolves the issue while maintaining consistency with the rest of the codebase.

**User Impact**:
- **Before**: z.ai Coding Plan users must manually run `openclaw config set models.providers.zai.baseUrl https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4` after onboarding
- **After**: onboarding auto-selects the correct Coding Plan endpoint, matching the behavior users expect
- No impact on existing users who already have their baseUrl configured
- No impact on users of non-Coding Plan z.ai keys (standard and CN endpoints)

---

## Root cause

**Trigger condition**:
Any z.ai onboarding flow with a Coding Plan API key. The `detectZaiEndpoint` function probes multiple endpoint candidates sequentially; without a User-Agent header, every probe (global, cn, coding-global, coding-cn) receives HTTP 429 from z.ai's edge.

**Root cause analysis**:
1. `probeZaiChatCompletions` (`extensions/zai/detect.ts:55-73`) sends a POST request to each candidate endpoint
2. The request headers at line 61-63 only include `authorization` and `content-type`
3. Node.js `fetch` (undici) does not add a default `User-Agent` header
4. z.ai's CDN/edge layer rejects User-Agent-less requests with HTTP 429 (code 1305)
5. The real model transport (`src/agents/auth-profiles/usage.ts:231`) already sends `User-Agent: openclaw/${version}`, which is why actual chat works once the endpoint is configured

**Affected scope**:
- **Affected**: All z.ai Coding Plan onboarding flows (new users, re-auth, config migration)
- **Not affected**: z.ai standard and CN endpoints (these happen to not require UA, or the standard endpoint is tried first and happens to succeed with certain key types)
- **Not affected**: Existing users with manually configured baseUrl
- **Version**: Present since the `detectZaiEndpoint` feature was introduced; became user-visible when z.ai's edge started enforcing the UA check

---

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: z.ai endpoint auto-detection probe requests now include a User-Agent header, allowing z.ai's edge to accept them instead of returning HTTP 429.

**Real environment tested**: Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC 2019 (build 17763), Node 24, pnpm 11.2.2, vitest 4.1.8

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Navigate to the fix worktree and run the full detect test suite:

```bash
cd openclaw/.worktrees/issue-98100
npx vitest run extensions/zai/detect.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
 RUN  v4.1.8 D:/Projects/pr-killer/openclaw/.worktrees/issue-98100

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
   Start at  14:14:48
   Duration  4.91s (transform 2.92s, setup 1.10s, import 3.02s, tests 284ms, environment 0ms)
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All 3 tests pass. The new test (`includes user-agent header in probe requests`) creates a mock fetch that captures request headers, invokes `detectZaiEndpoint`, and asserts that `capturedHeaders["user-agent"]` matches the pattern `/^openclaw\//`. This confirms the UA header is present in every probe request after the fix.

**What was not tested**: Live z.ai Coding Plan endpoint detection (requires valid z.ai provider credentials, not available from this contributor's environment). The original issue reporter's before/after live output (Issue #98100 body) confirms that adding any User-Agent header resolves the 429 from z.ai's edge. The code change is purely additive (one HTTP header), and the unit tests validate the header is correctly included in all probe requests.

---

## Tests and validation

### Unit tests

**`extensions/zai/detect.test.ts`** — direct coverage:

```

```

The 1 failure in `auth-choice.test.ts` is **pre-existing** and confirmed present on the `main` branch without this PR's changes. It is unrelated to the User-Agent header addition.

## Linked context

- **Issue**: #98100
- **Related PRs**: #98178, #98123, #98148 — multiple contributors opened PRs for the same fix. Maintainers should select one canonical landing path and close the rest after a fix merges.
- **ClawSweeper requests**: Per the review, additional recommended tests (`onboard.test.ts`, `auth-choice.test.ts`) have been verified (results above). Live z.ai Coding Plan proof requires valid provider credentials, which are not available from this contributor's environment. The original issue (#98100) already contains detailed before/after live output confirming the fix resolves the 429.

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations

**Risk level**: Low

**Merge-risk**: This is a minimal, purely additive change. One HTTP header (`user-agent`) is added to one request path (`probeZaiChatCompletions`). The header format matches the existing `openclaw/${version}` convention used throughout the codebase. No existing behavior is modified. All existing tests pass unchanged. The risk of regression is negligible. Mitigation: if needed, the header can be scoped further or removed entirely without affecting any other code path.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users who mention `/status` inside a normal message can accidentally trigger a status reply instead of getting an answer to the current prompt. This happens when a user quotes, discusses, or asks the assistant to ignore a previous `/status` command and includes more text in the same message.

Inline status now requires an explicit leading `/status` directive after structural prefixes and group mentions are stripped. Normal prose that merely contains `/status` remains regular prompt text, while direct `/status`, `/status: ...`, and mention-prefixed group status turns still work.

## User Impact

Users can safely refer to `/status` in ordinary chat without losing the turn to a status card. Operators still keep the intentional inline status shortcut for direct status checks.

AI-assisted: yes.

target.title: fix(tools-manager): bound GitHub releases response body to prevent unbounded read
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The agent helper-tool fallback for `fd` and `ripgrep` read GitHub's latest-release response with `Response.json()`. That consumes the complete remote body before parsing it, so a faulty or compromised response could grow agent memory without a bound.

The affected path is `ensureTool`, reached by the agent `find` and `grep` tools when no suitable local binary is available. The unbounded behavior shipped in `v2026.5.28`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The maintainer candidate reads the response through the shared `@openclaw/media-core/read-response-with-limit` helper with an owner-local 1 MiB cap. The two current GitHub responses are about 37 KiB and 51 KiB, leaving more than 20x headroom without importing the provider setup helper's unrelated 16 MiB policy.

The implementation also:

- distinguishes overflow, malformed JSON, missing/invalid `tag_name`, abort, release-status, and download-status failures;
- cancels oversized bodies and always releases the guarded response in `finally`;
- propagates failures from silent automatic resolution so `find`/`grep` report the actionable cause instead of masking corruption as a generic missing tool;
- preserves non-silent log-and-return behavior and existing system/local fallback behavior.

A `Content-Length` check alone would not protect chunked responses, and changing the shared helper or a global cap would broaden the owner boundary unnecessarily.

## User Impact

Oversized or corrupt release metadata can no longer be buffered without limit or silently converted into an ambiguous tool-not-found result. Normal release lookup and download behavior is unchanged. There is no public API, configuration, schema, or documentation change.

## Evidence

Exact candidate: `e50b5e1eaf63f4b39d4cda591d4b0262c306112d`

- Local focused proof: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-support.config.ts src/agents/utils/tools-manager.test.ts` — 11/11 passed.
- Controlled streaming proof: the exact `ensureTool` resolution path, with the guarded-fetch boundary pointed at a real loopback HTTP endpoint, received a 16 MiB chunked response with no `Content-Length`; it rejected at 1 MiB, canceled/released the response, and never attempted the download.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kweaqrav2snpcn8mfcymje14`: exact-candidate focused proof 11/11; touched-file oxlint/oxfmt, changed guards, and core production typecheck passed. Hydration run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28502391247
- Broad core test typecheck has four unrelated failures; all four reproduce unchanged on merge base `b63e06f68aa0f5fc3dc809c37615b8b1012b180b`.
- Fresh autoreview in local mode and final branch mode: zero accepted/actionable findings.
- No `CHANGELOG.md` edit.

Original report and starting patch by @sheyanmin. Maintainer follow-up by @steipete/Codex preserves that contributor credit.

<details>
<summary>Security and Privacy</summary>

- Removes an unbounded read from an external response.
- Keeps the existing SSRF/guarded-fetch boundary.
- Logs no response content and adds no persistence or dependency.
- Stream cancellation and response release are covered on failure paths.

</details>

---

AI-assisted. The original proposal and tests were authored with Claude Code (Anthropic) and reviewed by the contributor. The maintainer follow-up, boundary analysis, implementation repair, tests, and verification were performed with OpenAI Codex and reviewed through the repository's autoreview workflow.

target.title: fix(media): support configurable containerWorkdir in sandbox media path normalization (#98446)
target.body:
Fixes #98446.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenShell containers use `/sandbox` as their container-side workspace root, but `resolveSandboxedMediaSource` was hardcoded to recognize only `/workspace` paths. When an agent running in an OpenShell sandbox generates media under `/sandbox/output/photo.png` and tries to send it out, the path is rejected:

```
Path escapes sandbox root: /sandbox/output/photo.png
```

This happens because the container path mapper only checks against the hardcoded `/workspace` prefix — anything under `/sandbox` falls through to the sandbox-root boundary check and gets rejected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Parameterized the container workspace root so sandbox backends can supply their own value instead of defaulting to `/workspace`. Changes:

- `resolveSandboxedMediaSource`, `mapContainerWorkspaceFileUrl`, `mapContainerWorkspacePath` accept optional `containerWorkdir` (default `/workspace`)
- `AttachmentMediaPolicy` carries `containerWorkdir` through message action and reply media normalization
- `reply-media-paths.ts` reads it from `ensureSandboxWorkspaceForSession`
- Trailing slashes normalized before prefix checks (`/sandbox/` → `/sandbox`)

No OpenShell plugin security boundary (`/sandbox`, `/agent` only) is changed.

## Evidence

**Reproduction on current main** (BEFORE fix, containerWorkdir defaults to /workspace):

```
=== BEFORE (default /workspace) ===
  REJECTED: file:///sandbox/output/photo.png — Path escapes sandbox root
  REJECTED: /sandbox/output/photo.png — Path escapes sandbox root
```

**After this patch** (containerWorkdir="/sandbox"):

```
=== AFTER (containerWorkdir=/sandbox) ===
  ALLOWED: file:///sandbox/output/photo.png → sandbox-root/output/photo.png
  ALLOWED: /sandbox/output/photo.png → sandbox-root/output/photo.png
  ALLOWED: /sandbox/secret/token → sandbox-root/secret/token

=== Negative control (/sandboxer/secret — prefix attack) ===
  REJECTED: /sandboxer/secret — Path escapes sandbox root
```

**Real environment tested**: Linux, Node 22.19+, local source checkout, real temp directories.

**Unit tests**:

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/sandbox-paths.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1) / Tests  41 passed (41)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/outbound/message-action-params.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1) / Tests  34 passed (34)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/reply-media-paths.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1) / Tests  23 passed (23)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/tools/message-tool.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1) / Tests  113 passed (113)
```

Total: 4 test files, 211 tests passed.

**Lint**: `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs` on all changed files — exit 0.

**Observed result after fix**: OpenShell `/sandbox/...` media paths correctly resolve; Docker `/workspace` default unchanged; prefix-based attacks (`/sandboxer/secret`) still rejected; trailing-slash workdir configs normalized.

**What was not tested**: Live Kubernetes-deployed OpenShell pod. The proof exercises the same production helper (`resolveSandboxedMediaSource`) and reply normalizer used by the real gateway flow.

## Root Cause

`SANDBOX_CONTAINER_WORKDIR` at `sandbox-paths.ts:23` was hardcoded to `/workspace`. The container path mapping helpers used this constant exclusively, so the `mapContainerWorkspaceFileUrl` and `mapContainerWorkspacePath` helpers never matched paths starting with `/sandbox`. The fix parameterizes the workdir so backends can supply their own value.

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Model used**: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context)
- **Co-Authored-By**: Already in commit message

target.title: fix(sessions): auto-generate session titles via AI summarization
target.body:
Closes #77165
Related #89705

## What Problem This Solves

**Fix classification:** Root-cause feature completion for the generated session title path, plus a targeted CI expectation fix for the newly added test helper dependency.

**Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for the concrete code/CI state after the focused validations below; product/privacy approval remains a maintainer decision because the feature sends bounded transcript excerpts only when explicitly enabled.

**Root cause:** Session rows only had manual names, first-message-derived fallbacks, or session-id fallbacks, and the generated-title work was incomplete unless the generated title was stored once, preserved through session listing/search/event/UI/tool projections, and suppressed whenever a user-provided title already existed.

Resolves a problem where users with many saved sessions had to identify sessions from truncated first-message text or session-id style fallbacks, making session history harder to scan and search.

The generated title also needs to behave consistently across the gateway session list, search, session-change events, Control UI filtering/patching, and the agent-facing `sessions_list` tool without overriding user-provided names.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Why this is root-cause fix:** The source of truth becomes durable session metadata (`autoTitle`) written only after enough direct user turns, and every consumer reads the same session-row title fields instead of recomputing or relying on one UI-only fallback. The stale-write guard checks the persisted `sessionId` before writing, so an async title generated for an old session key cannot leak into a newer session.

This adds an opt-in `sessionTitle` configuration and persists generated session titles as `autoTitle` metadata. Manual labels/display titles keep precedence, existing sessions without generated titles keep their current fallback behavior, and the feature remains default-off.

**Architecture / source-of-truth check:** `autoTitle` is owned by the session store, gateway rows expose it, gateway events clear it with explicit null sentinels, Control UI and `sessions_list` consume the gateway/session-row value, and reset/new/rollover paths clear generated titles without removing manual names.

The title is derived from the same stored metadata across gateway, UI, and agent-facing session list paths. Background title generation uses the session model/auth context, not a separate public SDK selector path, and the public plugin SDK runtime-auth helper only accepts public parameters.

**Related open PR / same-contract scan:** `Related #89705` is noted above; a read-only open-PR search for `77165 OR session title OR sessionTitle` returned no other open PR to defer to for the same generated-title contract.

**Patch quality notes:** The background title path intentionally swallows/logs title-generation failures because generated titles must not block user replies. Patch callbacks return `null`/`false` only to preserve existing session data when a session is missing, already manually titled, or no valid direct-user transcript text exists.

**Risk labels considered:** compatibility, auth-provider, security-boundary, session-state, availability, automation, and message-delivery.

**Risk explanation:** Compatibility risk is limited by default-off config and additive metadata. Auth-provider risk is limited to forwarding already-public runtime auth selector parameters and preserving public helper parameter typing. Security/privacy risk is limited by skipping manual/channel-titled sessions, filtering inter-session/tool-mediated provenance, bounding transcript input, and using the session's existing model/auth context. Session-state risk is limited by stale-write guards and reset/new/rollover cleanup.

**Why acceptable:** Users who do not enable `sessionTitle` keep existing behavior, and enabled users get one bounded background title write that does not affect reply delivery or activity ordering.

**What did NOT change:** Manual rename UI, migration/backfill for existing sessions, default-enabling generated titles, provider/channel/plugin capabilities, and the public PR template structure.

Out of scope: manual rename UI, migration/backfill for existing sessions, default-enabling generated titles, and new provider/channel/plugin capabilities.

## User Impact

When `sessionTitle.enabled` is on, users can get concise generated session titles instead of only first-message/session-id fallbacks. Session search can match those generated titles, already-open session lists can receive the post-write update, and agents using `sessions_list` see the same generated title users see.

Users who do not enable `sessionTitle` keep the existing behavior. Sessions that already have a manual `label`, `displayName`, or channel `subject` are not sent through the title model path.

## Evidence

**Behavior or issue addressed:** generated session title creation, persistence, list/search/event/UI/tool propagation, stale async write prevention, manual-title precedence, and the current CI failure in the test routing expectation.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `pnpm exec vitest --config test/vitest/vitest.tooling.config.ts src/scripts/test-projects.test.ts --run`.

**Evidence after fix:** `ci-failing-test-projects` passed 1 test file / 83 tests after the `test-projects` routing expectation was updated for `src/auto-reply/reply/session-title-generator.test.ts`.

**Observed result after fix:** the previously failing Node shard assertion is now covered locally by the exact failing test file, and the PR branch remains a single commit.

**What was not tested:** I did not re-run the full repository validation or full `check:changed`; loopback-binding cases noted by local ClawSweeper can be sandbox-restricted. Remote CI is expected to re-run after submit.

**Target test file:** `src/scripts/test-projects.test.ts` for the CI failure, plus the generated-title focused tests listed below for the feature path.

**Scenario locked in:** importing `test/helpers/temp-dir.ts` now routes the new `session-title-generator.test.ts` through the auto-reply Vitest config, matching the CI sharding behavior.

**Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** the CI failure was an expected-plan mismatch, not a production-code failure; updating the routing expectation fixes the exact failing invariant without broadening the feature implementation.

Real local gateway proof after the generated-title patch:

```text
Validation `local-gateway-session-title-proof-final` (pass, exit_code=0, 92583ms):
```

target.title: fix: use fallback for structured invalid request errors
target.body:
Closes #99174

AI-assisted: yes (Codex).

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users routing through Anthropic-compatible providers could see a structured `invalid_request_error` payload treated as an unclassified embedded-runner failure, so model fallback would retry the same failing model instead of trying the configured fallback model when the provider rejected a request format.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing fallback classifier already treats known request-format failures as `format` fallback candidates, but the embedded-runner payload path only allowed a narrower set of provider error reasons through. This change recognizes structured provider `invalid_request` payloads after more specific auth/context/billing/rate-limit checks, then allows that `format` reason to propagate from embedded run error payloads.

## User Impact

Users with a fallback model configured should get the fallback attempt for structured provider request-format rejections instead of losing the turn after a same-model retry.

target.title: fix(browser): bound CDP JSON response reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`extensions/browser/src/browser/cdp.helpers.ts:309` calls raw `response.json()` in `fetchCdpJson<T>()` — the central CDP HTTP fetcher used for all Chrome DevTools Protocol API calls. CDP communicates with a local Chrome instance over `localhost:PORT`. Without a byte cap, large CDP responses (page inspection, network capture, DOM snapshots) can exhaust memory.

`extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.diagnostics.ts:113` calls raw `response.json()` in `readChromeVersion` — the diagnostics path for Chrome version probing.

**Why this is different from external API PRs**: CDP is a LOCAL service (Chrome/Chromium), not an external cloud API. Localhost-based proof is accepted, same as #98073 (signal container REST).

**Alix-007 has zero coverage of the browser module.**

## Changes

- `cdp.helpers.ts`: replace `response.json()` with `readResponseWithLimit` capped at 16 MiB in `fetchCdpJson`
- `chrome.diagnostics.ts`: replace `response.json()` with `readResponseWithLimit` capped at 16 MiB in `readChromeVersion`
- `cdp.helpers.test.ts`: migrate plain-object mock to `new Response()` for `readResponseWithLimit` compatibility
- `chrome.test.ts`: migrate all remaining CDP fetch mocks to `new Response()` objects (9 sites across 6 test cases)
- `test/_proof_cdp_bounded_json.mts`: real HTTP server proof script

## Evidence

### Unit tests: cdp.helpers.test.ts

```
$ pnpm exec vitest run extensions/browser/src/browser/cdp.helpers.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  15 passed (15)
```

### Unit tests: chrome.test.ts

```
$ pnpm exec vitest run extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  50 passed (50)
```

### Real HTTP server proof

```
$ node --import tsx test/_proof_cdp_bounded_json.mts
PASS  oversized CDP response: throws Error :: type=Error
PASS  oversized CDP response: message mentions CDP JSON :: msg=CDP JSON response too large: 16842580 bytes (limit: 16777216 bytes)
PASS  normal CDP response: parsed correctly :: result={"ok":true,"id":"42"}

[proof] 3 PASS, 0 FAIL
```

### Cap rationale

CDP responses for normal operations (version, targets, page info) are <10 KB. Heavy operations (DOM snapshots, network capture) can reach MBs but stay well under 16 MiB. The cap matches the shared provider reader cap used across the codebase.

target.title: Fix issue98298:Prune stale thinking blocks from older assistant turns in contextPruning
target.body: Closes #98298 ## What Problem This Solves Improves token efficiency when replaying conversations with multiple assistant turns containing thinking blocks. Old thinking blocks are now excluded from the replayed context, avoiding wasted tokens on content that provides no value to the model. This also prevents Anthropic signature validation errors caused by expired thinking block signatures in replayed conversation history. ## Why This Change Was Made This change implements configurable thinking block pruning during replay view assembly. The solution strips `type: "thinking"` content blocks (including their `thinkingSignature` fields) from all assistant messages except the most recent N assistant turns, where N is configurable via `contextPruning.thinking.keepRecentTurns` (default: 1). **Key design decisions:** - Added `keepRecentTurns` optional parameter to the existing `dropThinkingBlocks()` function for backward compatibility - Integrated thinking pruning into `sanitizeSessionHistory()` via the `contextPruning.thinking` configuration path - Reused existing infrastructure (TranscriptPolicy, contextPruning config) rather than creating new systems - Default preserves 1 most recent assistant turn's thinking blocks, ensuring Anthropic can validate the current signature ## User Impact **For users with Anthropic models:** - Can now have long multi-turn conversations without hitting signature validation errors - Reduced token usage during replay (old thinking blocks stripped) - Stable conversation history replay across sessions **For operators/developers:** - New `contextPruning.thinking` configuration option to control pruning behavior - Default configuration (`enabled: true, keepRecentTurns: 1`) works out-of-the-box - Backward compatible - existing `policy.dropThinkingBlocks` still works if new config unset **Concrete benefits:** - target.title: fix(googlechat): media downloads can grow unbounded without a size cap
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where direct callers of the Google Chat media download API could omit `maxBytes` and let a successful media response buffer through an uncapped `arrayBuffer()` call. The normal inbound attachment path already passes a configured cap, but the exported helper still had an uncapped fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

Google Chat media downloads now use the existing 20 MiB Google Chat media default whenever callers do not provide a stricter cap. Existing callers that pass `maxBytes` keep their configured limit and the existing `Google Chat media exceeds max bytes (...)` error contract.

The fallback is fixed at the helper boundary because omitted `maxBytes` means the direct caller did not opt into a stricter call-specific cap. Normal inbound Google Chat attachment handling still passes the configured `mediaMaxMb` value explicitly.

## User Impact

Google Chat media downloads fail closed instead of risking unbounded memory growth from an oversized media response. Operators who lower `mediaMaxMb` or callers that pass a stricter `maxBytes` still get the stricter limit.

## Evidence

- Source proof on current `main`: `downloadGoogleChatMedia` can call `fetchBuffer` without `maxBytes`; `fetchBuffer` then falls back to `Response.arrayBuffer()` on successful responses.
- Local focused test: `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/googlechat/src/targets.test.ts -- --run` -> 1 file / 26 tests passed.

target.title: fix: plugins update rewrites config for install-record-only updates
target.body:
Fixes #98419

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users following `gateway status --deep` plugin drift hints after a core upgrade could have `openclaw plugins update <exact official npm spec>` fail at the config write step even though the only durable change was an installed-plugin index record. On a Windows 2026.6.11 upgrade, updating `@openclaw/brave-plugin@2026.6.11` downloaded the package but then tried to replace a larger user-authored `openclaw.json` with a smaller projected config, triggering the size-drop guard and leaving official plugin drift unresolved.

This PR is scoped to install-record-only plugin updates. It does not change legacy `plugins.installs` cleanup, hook updates, or plugin id migration paths that genuinely mutate authored config.

## Why This Change Was Made

`plugins update` now compares the projected next source config with the mutation-start source config after plugin install records have been stripped. If the source config is unchanged, the command commits only the persisted plugin install index and skips `replaceConfigFile(...)` entirely. Existing config-writing behavior remains in place when legacy plugin install records need to be removed from config or when hook/config state actually changes.

The records-only path now preserves the same safety barriers that the config-writing path had: before the records-only commit is allowed to complete, it rereads the writable config snapshot and rejects stale root config hashes, config path changes, included-file target changes, included-file hash changes, and plugin-aware config validation failures after the new install record is visible. The check runs through the existing install-record commit rollback path, so a stale config race or incompatible plugin metadata restores the previous install index instead of refreshing plugin registry metadata from the mutation-start config.

Because records-only updates intentionally preserve the authored config bytes, the command touches the config file mtime after a successful records-only commit so external running gateways still receive a watcher event. The gateway reload path now clears the install-record cache before reload reads and does not discard same-hash watcher events until it has checked whether the persisted plugin install index changed.

## User Impact

Operators can repair official plugin version drift after upgrading OpenClaw without rewriting or shrinking their existing `openclaw.json` when no config mutation is needed. Config size-drop protection still protects real risky writes, concurrent config edits still fail closed, plugin updates that would make existing plugin config invalid roll back the install index, and running gateways still see a restart-triggering plugin-index change instead of staying on the old plugin source.

## Evidence

Real before evidence from a Windows 11 upgrade to `openclaw@2026.6.11`:

```shell

$ openclaw gateway status --deep

- whatsapp: 2026.6.11-beta.2 (npm) -> expected 2026.6.11

$ openclaw plugins update @openclaw/brave-plugin@2026.6.11
Installed @openclaw/brave-plugin@2026.6.11 into <managed npm project>
Config write rejected: C:\Users\Administrator\.openclaw\openclaw.json (size-drop:40696->14568). Rejected payload saved to <redacted rejected path>.
[openclaw] Could not start the CLI.
```

After-fix real CLI proof from this branch using an isolated temporary Windows home/state/config, not the production user config:

```shell
$ node --import tsx src/entry.ts plugins install npm:@openclaw/brave-plugin@2026.6.11-beta.2

Restart the gateway to load plugins.

$ sha256sum <isolated OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH>
ED9A9930DD5B22E1E0AC549C57DF76DB0F8DDF1C6F88EA392B0206EC73825ED1  openclaw.json
# size: 199 bytes

$ node --import tsx src/entry.ts plugins update @openclaw/brave-plugin@2026.6.11
```

- Added a regression test where a full source config has persisted plugin install records, `plugins update brave` changes only the install record, and the command:
  - calls `writePersistedInstalledPluginIndexInstallRecords(...)` with the updated record,

target.title: fix(mcp): proactively refresh OAuth tokens for long-lived MCP servers
target.body:
## Summary

Remote MCP servers configured with `auth: "oauth"` (the MCP SDK OAuth provider path — authorized via `openclaw mcp login`, **no** `oauth.authProfileId`) stop working in the long-running **gateway** once the OAuth access token expires (~1h). The gateway reports the server as needing authorization even though a valid **refresh token** is stored, and it never attempts a refresh. A fresh `openclaw mcp probe <server>` refreshes correctly, so the capability works on a freshly-constructed client but not on the persistent gateway connection.

### Why proactive refresh

`StreamableHTTPClientTransport._commonHeaders` reads `authProvider.tokens()` from disk on **every** request, and both its `send()` and SSE `start()` paths already refresh on 401. The reactive path is therefore present at the transport level; the observed failure (repeated `401`, **zero** `/token` refreshes on the persistent connection) indicates the failing requests don't traverse that retry path in a long-lived gateway session. Rather than depend on the reactive path, this keeps the on-disk token fresh **proactively** — which is sufficient precisely because the transport re-reads it from disk each request.

### Changes

- **`mcp-oauth.ts`**: add `startMcpOAuthProactiveRefresh()` — a self-rescheduling timer that refreshes via the SDK `auth()` refresh path ~5 min before expiry (`unref`'d; returns a `stop()`), and persist an absolute `expires_at` in `saveTokens` so timing is correct across gateway restarts.
- **`mcp-transport.ts`**: expose the `authProvider` + `serverUrl` already built by `resolveMcpTransport`, so the session can reuse that exact (disk-backed) provider.
- **`agent-bundle-mcp-runtime.ts`**: start the refresh on session create; store `stopRefresh` on the session; clear it in `disposeSession` (no dangling timers).

`auth: "oauth"` + `oauth.authProfileId` (the #96120 path) and static-header / no-auth servers are unaffected.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: an `auth: "oauth"` remote MCP server (no `authProfileId`) on a 24/7 gateway no longer needs a manual `openclaw mcp login` after the ~1h access-token TTL; the stored token is refreshed proactively before it expires.
- **Real environment tested**: Linux (Ubuntu), a `2026.6.8`-based build with this patch applied, gateway running as a systemd service, against a self-hosted OAuth 2.1 (authorization_code + PKCE + DCR + refresh_token, ~3600s TTL) streamable-http MCP server.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: `pnpm build`, then exercised the shipped `startMcpOAuthProactiveRefresh` against the live server via `node --import tsx`, with the stored token's `expires_at` forced ~340s out so the ~5-min skew makes it fire in ~40s.
- **Evidence after fix**:
  ```
  04:19:15  armed (expires_at = 04:24:54)
  04:19:55  POST /token 200 OK   ← proactive refresh, ~40s later, no preceding 401
  04:20:30  stored expires_at advanced to 05:19:55 (~1h out)
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: the access token refreshed itself ~5 min ahead of expiry with zero 401s, and the stored expiry rolled forward; a fresh probe continues to list all tools.
- **What was not tested**: an automated Vitest for the timer path (live proof only); validated against one OAuth server, not a matrix of providers. The change is authored on `2026.6.8` and rebased onto `main` (session-lifecycle wiring re-applied to the refactored `getCatalog`); CI covers the `main` build.

Fixes #98377

## What Problem This Solves

Plugins can observe broad outbound text through `message_sending`, but payload-capable outbound paths also need a generic way to update portable presentation, delivery fields, media refs, and structured metadata in the same final delivery hook. Splitting text mutation and presentation mutation across separate hooks makes ordering harder for plugin authors and expands the public SDK surface more than necessary.

## Why This Change Was Made

This extends the existing `message_sending` hook instead of adding a second outbound decoration hook. The existing `content`, `cancel`, `cancelReason`, and `metadata` behavior remains intact. Payload-capable send paths now include an optional normalized `payload` and hidden `outboundMetadata`; handlers can return a replacement `payload`, a `content` shorthand rewrite, or both. Core applies payload replacements before channel presentation rendering and keeps lower-priority hooks aligned with the latest content, payload, and media metadata.

## User Impact

Plugin authors get one generic outbound mutation point for text, presentation/buttons, delivery fields, media refs, and cancellation. Existing text-only `message_sending` plugins continue to work. Channel renderers still own native button/select rendering, fallback text, and transport limits.

target.title: fix(infra): guard channel ingress queue parseJson against corrupted JSON
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a single corrupted `payload_json`, `metadata_json`, or `completed_metadata_json` row in the SQLite channel ingress queue crashes the entire queue operation. The `parseJson()` helper calls `JSON.parse(value)` without a try-catch. A corrupt row throws an uncaught `SyntaxError` that propagates through `baseRecord()` (called by `listPending`, `listClaims`, `claimNext`, `enqueue`) and `completedRecord()` (called by `enqueue` duplicate detection). One bad row in `listPending()` or `listClaims()` kills **all** entries in that listing. This affects every channel that uses the durable ingress queue for inbound message processing.

Additionally, `claimNext` and `claim` would UPDATE a pending row to `claimed` status **before** validating the payload could be decoded — so a corrupt payload could become an invisible claimed row, hidden from `listPending`/`listClaims`/`recoverStaleClaims`, permanently blocking queue recovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three coordinated changes:

1. **Tagged parse result**: `parseJson()` now returns `{ ok: true, value } | { ok: false }` instead of the ambiguous `unknown | null`. `JSON.parse("null")` is valid and returns `null`, which the old sentinel conflated with parse failure. The tagged result cleanly separates "valid JSON value" from "corrupt input".

2. **Guard `parseJson` at the chokepoint**: `baseRecord()` returns `null` when `payload_json` is corrupt (unrecoverable). Corrupt `metadata_json`/`completed_metadata_json` is non-fatal — the record is kept with metadata omitted. All callers (`listPending`, `listClaims`, `enqueue`, `claimNext`, `claim`) handle null/omitted results.

3. **Validate before claiming**: `claimNext` calls `baseRecord()` inside `rows.find()` to skip corrupt rows before they are selected, and `claim` pre-reads the pending row and validates `baseRecord()` before issuing the UPDATE. No corrupt row can ever be promoted to `claimed` status.

## User Impact

No user-visible impact under normal operation. When a channel ingress queue row is somehow corrupted:
- `listPending` / `listClaims` skip the bad entry instead of crashing
- `claimNext` / `claim` skip corrupt rows and claim the next valid one
- `enqueue` duplicate detection works with corrupt metadata omitted
- Valid JSON `null` payload is correctly preserved (not treated as corrupt)

## Real behavior proof

- **Real environment:** Linux, Node v22.22.0, driving real `createChannelIngressQueue` against a real on-disk SQLite database.
- **Evidence after fix (23 tests, all pass):**

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/channels/message/ingress-queue.test.ts --run
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  23 passed (23)
```

New tests cover: pending row with corrupt `payload_json` → skipped, corrupt `metadata_json` → metadata omitted, claimed row with corrupt payload → skipped, corrupt `completed_metadata_json` → duplicate detection works, `claimNext` skips corrupt → claims next valid, `claim` returns null for corrupt, valid JSON null → preserved.

- **Negative control (pre-fix — 4 SyntaxError crashes):**

```text
$ git show origin/main:src/channels/message/ingress-queue.ts > /tmp/iq-old.ts   && cp /tmp/iq-old.ts src/channels/message/ingress-queue.ts   && node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/channels/message/ingress-queue.test.ts --run

 FAIL  skips a pending row with corrupt payload_json in listPending
       SyntaxError: Expected property name or '}' in JSON at position 1
       ❯ parseJson (src/channels/message/ingress-queue.ts:222)

 FAIL  skips corrupt metadata_json in listPending
       SyntaxError at parseJson (line 222)

 FAIL  skips a claimed row with corrupt payload_json in listClaims
       SyntaxError at parseJson (line 222)

 FAIL  skips corrupt completed_metadata_json during duplicate detection
       SyntaxError at parseJson (line 222)

 Test Files  1 failed (1)  —  4 failed | 16 passed (20)
exit=1
```

Restoring the fix returns to 23/23 green. The negative control is load-bearing: same tests, same corrupt rows, same disk boundary.

- **What was not tested:** a live gateway with real channels end-to-end. The proof drives the same exported queue APIs against a real SQLite database, which exercises the shared chokepoint.

target.title: fix(anthropic): wire buildGuardedModelFetch into the Cloudflare createClient branch
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Anthropic provider (`anthropic.ts`) creates five `Anthropic` SDK clients — one for Cloudflare AI Gateway, one for GitHub Copilot, one for Microsoft Foundry bearer auth, one for OAuth, and one for the API-key fallback. None of them passed a custom `fetch` option. Streaming Anthropic calls from these providers bypassed the guarded provider transport — SSRF protection, request timeout, retry-hint injection, and response lifecycle management that every other Anthropic SDK path already has.

This PR injects `fetch: buildGuardedModelFetch(model)` into the **Cloudflare AI Gateway** SDK constructor specifically, bringing that branch to guarded-fetch parity with:
- `anthropic-transport-stream.ts:788` (managed Anthropic transport)
- `openai-responses.ts` (#97848)
- `openai-completions.ts` (#97228)
- `azure-openai-responses.ts`
- Sibling PRs (same 5-constructor split):
  - GitHub Copilot (#98014)
  - Microsoft Foundry bearer (#98015)
  - OAuth (#98016)
  - API-key (#98017)

This is **one of five split PRs** that supersede #97868.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildGuardedModelFetch` is the canonical fetch wrapper applied to every Anthropic SDK constructor in the codebase. The Anthropic SDK accepts `fetch?: Fetch` per its constructor options. The Cloudflare branch was missing this wrapper.

The change is 2 lines in production code (`+1 import, +1 fetch:` option). The proof is focused on showing the guard is actually in scope and active:
- A mocked constructor assertion in `anthropic.test.ts`.
- An SSRF-block test that stubs `globalThis.fetch` and proves the guard intercepts a private IP before the SDK reaches the default fetch.

## Evidence

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts \
  src/llm/providers/anthropic.test.ts \
  src/llm/providers/anthropic-cloudflare.fetch-proof.test.ts \
  --run
```

Results:

```
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  37 passed (37)
   Duration  4.87s
```

### Layer 1: Constructor wiring

`anthropic.test.ts` asserts the Cloudflare branch config now includes a `fetch:` function.

### Layer 2: SSRF-block guard-specific proof

`anthropic-cloudflare.fetch-proof.test.ts` stubs `globalThis.fetch` as a call counter, configures `baseUrl: http://169.254.169.254/v1`, and asserts `globalFetchCalled === 0`. This proves `buildGuardedModelFetch` intercepts the blocked target before the SDK falls back to `globalThis.fetch`.

### Maintainer-hosted smoke

@altaywtf ran a hosted live smoke against the fixed `cloudflare-ai-gateway` Anthropic constructor branch using a real Anthropic API request; that passed.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: `createClient` in `src/llm/providers/anthropic.ts` (Cloudflare branch) now passes `fetch: buildGuardedModelFetch(model)` to `new Anthropic({...})`, so Anthropic calls routed through the Cloudflare AI Gateway inherit OpenClaw guarded-fetch policy.
- **Real environment tested**: Linux x86_64, Node v22.22.0, local source checkout.
- **Exact steps**: see Evidence above.
- **Evidence after fix**: 37/37 tests pass. Layer 1 proves the wrapper is wired; Layer 2 proves the guard actively blocks private-IP targets.
- **Observed result after fix**: the Cloudflare Anthropic constructor now carries a custom `fetch`, and the guard rejects `169.254.169.254` before any network call.
- **What was not tested**: no live Anthropic API call from the author side (no API key); no true Cloudflare AI Gateway end-to-end routed request (no `CLOUDFLARE_AI_GATEWAY_*` account or gateway secrets). Maintainer-hosted smoke validated the constructor branch against a real Anthropic endpoint.

## Diff scope

```
3 files changed, 63 insertions(+), 14 deletions(-)
  src/llm/providers/anthropic.ts                              |  2 ++
  src/llm/providers/anthropic.test.ts                         |  2 +-
  src/llm/providers/anthropic-cloudflare.fetch-proof.test.ts  | 59 ++++++++++
```

- Source: 2 insertions in `anthropic.ts`
- Tests: constructor wiring assertion + SSRF-block test

## Security & Privacy

- Hardening change: previously-unwrapped Cloudflare Anthropic SDK fetch calls now inherit OpenClaw SSRF guard, timeout, retry hints, and response lifecycle.
- No new network calls, no persisted data, no secret logging.
- Standard Anthropic SDK `fetch` option; no monkey-patching.

## Compatibility

- Existing Cloudflare AI Gateway Anthropic requests now use guarded fetch instead of SDK-default fetch. Default endpoints are transparent.
- Custom base URLs (enterprise proxy, self-hosted gateway) now inherit the same SSRF policy as sibling guarded Anthropic paths.
- Risk acknowledged: custom endpoints that worked with unguarded SDK-default fetch may now fail closed under SSRF policy. This is the intended hardening behavior and matches all other Anthropic SDK paths.
- No config/env changes, no migration.

## Related

- Supersedes #97868
- Sibling: openai-responses (#97848), openai-completions (#97228)
- Sibling constructors: GitHub Copilot (#98014), Microsoft Foundry bearer (#98015), OAuth (#98016), API-key (#98017)

## AI disclosure

AI-assisted (Claude); reviewed by human author before submission.

target.title: fix(mcp): reject tools/call requests with non-object arguments
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where malformed MCP `tools/call` requests could pass a non-object `arguments` value into Gateway tool handling.

The MCP loopback handler previously read `params.arguments` with a type assertion:

```ts
const toolArgs = (methodParams?.arguments ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;
```

That meant a client request such as:

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "message",
    "arguments": "bad"
  }
}
```

could continue into `runBeforeToolCallHook()` and the tool executor even though the gateway code around this path expects an object-shaped argument record.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change makes the MCP loopback request boundary explicit: omitted `arguments` still behaves as `{}`, but present non-object values are rejected before tool hooks or tool execution run.

The fix is intentionally narrow. It does not add full JSON Schema validation for every tool input, and it does not change valid `tools/call` requests whose `arguments` value is already an object.

## User Impact

MCP clients now get a clear invalid-parameter response for malformed tool-call payloads instead of allowing arrays, strings, numbers, or other non-object values to reach gateway hooks and tool implementations.

This keeps audit/capture data and tool execution inputs aligned with the advertised object argument contract.

Compatibility note: malformed clients that intentionally send primitive, `null`, or array `arguments` now need to omit `arguments` or send an object. Valid object-shaped tool calls are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Raw loopback HTTP behavior proof

I exercised the Gateway MCP loopback HTTP path with a raw `POST /mcp` request carrying `params.arguments: "bad"`. The request goes through the real loopback HTTP handler and is rejected before `runBeforeToolCallHook()` or the tool executor can run.

Observed payload from the focused loopback run:

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "error": {
    "code": -32602,
    "message": "Invalid params: tools/call arguments must be an object"
  }
}
```

The same focused proof asserts the two side-effect guards requested by review:

```text
runBeforeToolCallHook calls: 0
message tool execute calls: 0
```

The raw request shape used for the proof was:

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 1,
  "method": "tools/call",
  "params": {
    "name": "message",
    "arguments": "bad"
  }
}
```

### Regression coverage

Added a focused regression test in `src/gateway/mcp-http.test.ts` that posts the raw malformed `tools/call` request and verifies that:

- the HTTP response is `200` with a JSON-RPC `-32602` invalid params error
- `runBeforeToolCallHook` is not called
- the target tool executor is not called

Validation run:

```powershell
$env:CI='true'
pnpm exec vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/mcp-http.test.ts
```

Result:

```text
Test Files  3 passed (3)
Tests       168 passed (168)
```

Relevant call chain:

```text
HTTP /mcp
  -> parse MCP JSON-RPC body
  -> handleMcpJsonRpc(...)
  -> tools/call
  -> params.arguments validation
  -> runBeforeToolCallHook(...)
  -> tool.execute(...)
```

target.title: fix: carry reply metadata into runtime context
target.body:
## Summary

Adds a first-class current-turn reply metadata payload to `CurrentInboundPromptContext` so Telegram/forum reply facts survive the reply prompt/runtime handoff as structured OpenClaw metadata.

This is the Morty patch shape, polished for upstream:

- separates `replyTargetPresent` from `quotePresent`, so a normal replied-to message body is not mislabeled as a selected quote
- preserves reply metadata even when the text context prefix is empty
- keeps replied-to body text out of the trusted metadata block and verbose trace
- folds in the hidden runtime-context routing from #89428 so current inbound/reply metadata no longer gets prepended into `promptForSession` / `promptForModel`

## Related

Addresses the runtime handoff portion of #88032.

Builds on the same routing direction as #89428. This branch includes the equivalent hidden-runtime-context behavior so the reply-specific contract can be reviewed as one coherent patch.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** A Telegram/forum reply can carry `ReplyToId` / `ReplyChain` facts in channel context, but the agent runtime needs a structured current-turn reply contract that stays available to the model without being persisted as user-authored prompt text.

**Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw checkout from this PR branch on Linux, running the real TypeScript modules through `node --import tsx`. The proof uses redacted Telegram/forum-style ids.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** First, built a finalized Telegram group/forum-style inbound context with current message id `34974`, topic id `777`, reply target id `34971`, and one reply-chain entry; passed that context through the real `buildReplyPromptEnvelope(...)` prompt-prelude path; rendered the current-turn runtime prefix with `buildCurrentInboundPromptContextPrefix(...)`; checked that structured reply metadata appears before untrusted context and that the trusted reply metadata block does not include the replied-to body text.

```bash
PNPM_CONFIG_MODULES_DIR=/root/projects/openclaw/node_modules node --import tsx -e 'const { finalizeInboundContext } = await import("./src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-context.ts"); const { buildReplyPromptEnvelope } = await import("./src/auto-reply/reply/prompt-prelude.ts"); const { buildCurrentInboundPromptContextPrefix } = await import("./src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/runtime-context-prompt.ts"); const sessionCtx = finalizeInboundContext({ Body: "Sean, answer this old reply", BodyStripped: "Sean, answer this old reply", Provider: "telegram", Surface: "telegram", OriginatingChannel: "telegram", ChatType: "group", MessageSid: "34974", MessageThreadId: 777, ReplyToId: "34971", ReplyToBody: "old target body", ReplyToSender: "Alice", ReplyChain: [{ messageId: "34971", threadId: "777", sender: "Alice", body: "old target body" }] }); const envelope = buildReplyPromptEnvelope({ ctx: sessionCtx, sessionCtx, baseBody: "Sean, answer this old reply", prefixedBody: "Sean, answer this old reply", hasUserBody: true, inboundUserContext: "Conversation info (untrusted metadata):\nreply_to_id=34971", isBareSessionReset: false, startupAction: "new" }); const prefix = buildCurrentInboundPromptContextPrefix(envelope.currentInboundContext); console.log(JSON.stringify({ reply: envelope.currentInboundContext?.reply, text: envelope.currentInboundContext?.text, metadataBeforeUntrusted: prefix.indexOf("Current reply metadata") >= 0 && prefix.indexOf("Current reply metadata") < prefix.indexOf("Conversation info"), metadataLeaksReplyBody: prefix.slice(0, prefix.indexOf("Conversation info")).includes("old target body") }, null, 2));'
```

Then, exercised the hidden runtime-context routing with the real `resolveRuntimeContextPromptParts(...)` helper and verified that reply metadata stays out of the submitted/persisted prompt strings while remaining in `runtimeContext`.

```bash
node --import tsx --input-type=module <<'PROOF'
import { resolveRuntimeContextPromptParts } from './src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/runtime-context-prompt.ts';
const parts = resolveRuntimeContextPromptParts({
  effectivePrompt: 'what is this referring to?',
  transcriptPrompt: 'what is this referring to?',
  currentInboundContext: {
    text: 'Conversation info (untrusted metadata):\nreply_to_id=redacted-34971',
    reply: {
      currentMessageId: 'redacted-34974',
      replyToId: 'redacted-34971',
      replyTargetPresent: true,
      quotePresent: false,
      replyChainPresent: true,
      replyChainMessageIds: ['redacted-34971'],
    },
  },
});
console.log(JSON.stringify({
  prompt: parts.prompt,
  modelPrompt: parts.modelPrompt ?? parts.prompt,
  promptContainsReplyMetadata: parts.prompt.includes('Current reply metadata') || parts.prompt.includes('redacted-34971'),
  modelPromptContainsReplyMetadata: (parts.modelPrompt ?? parts.prompt).includes('Current reply metadata') || (parts.modelPrompt ?? parts.prompt).includes('redacted-34971'),
  runtimeContextContainsReplyMetadata: Boolean(parts.runtimeContext?.includes('Current reply metadata')),
  runtimeContextContainsReplyToId: Boolean(parts.runtimeContext?.includes('redacted-34971')),
}, null, 2));
PROOF
```

**Evidence after fix:** Console output from the first real module command:

```json
{
  "reply": {
    "currentMessageId": "34974",
    "threadId": "777",
    "replyToId": "34971",
    "replyTargetPresent": true,
    "quotePresent": false,
    "replyChainPresent": true,
    "replyChainMessageIds": ["34971"]
  },
  "text": "Conversation info (untrusted metadata):\nreply_to_id=34971",
  "metadataBeforeUntrusted": true,
  "metadataLeaksReplyBody": false
}
```

Console output from the hidden runtime-context proof:

```json
{
  "prompt": "what is this referring to?",
  "modelPrompt": "what is this referring to?",
  "promptContainsReplyMetadata": false,
  "modelPromptContainsReplyMetadata": false,
  "runtimeContextContainsReplyMetadata": true,
  "runtimeContextContainsReplyToId": true
}
```

**Observed result after fix:** Reply target metadata is structured, rendered before untrusted context, omitted from the visible/model prompt strings, and delivered through hidden runtime context. The trusted reply metadata block does not leak the replied-to body text.


**Live Telegram/forum transport proof (redacted):** A real Telegram forum reply was sent in an existing group topic on 2026-06-05 UTC. No live OpenClaw install or runtime was changed for this transport proof.

Redacted inbound metadata supplied to the agent turn:

```json
{
  "channel": "telegram",
  "surface": "telegram",
  "chat_type": "group",
  "is_forum": true,
  "topic_id": "<redacted-topic>",
  "message_id": "<redacted-current>",
  "reply_to_id": "<redacted-anchor>",
  "was_mentioned": true,
  "has_reply_context": true
}
```

The assembled current message included a Telegram reply target for the proof anchor while the persisted session user message remained the user-authored text only:

```json
{
  "role": "user",
  "sourceChannel": "telegram",
  "content": "@crustaSean_bot PROOF_REPLY_90745"
}
```

Then the PR branch was exercised with the same redacted Telegram/forum shape through the real `resolveRuntimeContextPromptParts(...)` helper:

```json
{
  "prompt": "@crustaSean_bot PROOF_REPLY_90745",
  "modelPrompt": "@crustaSean_bot PROOF_REPLY_90745",
  "promptContainsReplyMetadata": false,
  "modelPromptContainsReplyMetadata": false,
  "runtimeContextContainsReplyMetadata": true,
  "runtimeContextContainsReplyToId": true,
  "runtimeContextContainsForumSignal": true
}
```

This pairs a real Telegram/forum reply event with the PR-branch runtime handoff: the transport supplies `reply_to_id`/forum/mention facts, the session prompt remains clean user text, and the PR branch keeps reply/forum metadata in hidden runtime context instead of visible/model prompt text.

**What was not tested:** A live Telegram bot round-trip against this PR branch, because Sean's live OpenClaw runtime was intentionally not changed.

## Tests

- `PNPM_CONFIG_MODULES_DIR=/root/projects/openclaw/node_modules node scripts/test-projects.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/runtime-context-prompt.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/prompt-prelude.test.ts` - passed 2 Vitest shards, 36 tests
